Wider Sports News.summary: Kyadondo Rugby Grounds to host Rugby Africa HSBC Division III Qualifier Kawowo Sports
Wider Sports News.body:
Kyadondo Rugby Grounds will host the Rugby Africa HSBC Division III qualifiers scheduled for September 26-27 in Kampala, Uganda. The tournament is set to attract 8 men’s teams from across Africa for 2 days of mouth-watering sevens rugby at the de facto home of Ugandan Rugby.

This tournament was set up after the split from the Rugby Africa 7s, which will happen in Mauritius from October 3 to 4. Wider Sports News.title: Why Big Bash League franchises are up for sale and what it means for franchise cricket
Wider Sports News.summary: After falling short with a proposal earlier this year, Cricket Australia is pushing on with plans to sell stakes in its Big Bash League teams. The post Why Big Bash League franchises are up for sale and what it means for franchise cricket appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The boundaries of franchise cricket investment have been redrawn once again, circling another of the sport’s big three markets. Cricket Australia (CA) has confirmed plans to offer stakes to private investors in the eight teams from its domestic T20 competitions, the Big Bash League (BBL) and Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL).

Last week the organisation announced that its member bodies – each representing one of the six Australian states – could make their own decisions on selling shares under a ‘self-determination model’. The hope is that this raises up to AUS$1 billion (US$710 million) in fresh capital, most likely from groups with financial interests in Indian Premier League (IPL) teams and elsewhere on the global T20 circuit.

Wider Sports News.title: Liverpool’s UK£300m shirt deal shows airlines are doubling down on sponsorship – but who will it actually reach?
Wider Sports News.summary: The Space Between co-founder Adam Raincock on why Turkish Airlines' record Liverpool sponsorship doesn't guarantee access to the club's global audience. The post Liverpool’s UK£300m shirt deal shows airlines are doubling down on sponsorship – but who will it actually reach? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Last week, Liverpool reset the market for Premier League shirt sponsorship by announcing a record-breaking five-year deal with Turkish Airlines worth a reported UK£60 million (US$80 million) annually.

At a time when many categories are reassessing marketing spend, the airline sector is moving in the opposite direction, doubling down on sport and football in particular. Turkish Airlines is far from alone. Emirates has built a large part of its brand on the world’s most recognisable sponsorship assets through long-term partnerships with Arsenal, Real Madrid and a portfolio of major sporting events. Qatar Airways has invested heavily across football’s biggest properties, while Etihad continues to use Manchester City as a key pillar of its global marketing.

Wider Sports News.body:
Netflix, Amazon and YouTube have formed a new industry body designed to represent streaming services amid ongoing criticism about the rising cost of watching live sport in the US.

The Streaming Access and Choice Alliance (SACA) will be led by TechNet, a technology industry trade group comprising 106 members, and lobby lawmakers and regulators who have suggested measures designed to keep sport on linear television could be introduced to protect consumers.

Udine, 15th September 2026 – Udinese Calcio today announced the launch of Play for Sustainability – Our Planet, Our Game, a new annual initiative designed to integrate measurable sustainability actions into the delivery of a Serie A matchday. The initiative was presented at a press conference held at the Bluenergy Stadium with representatives from UEFA, Lega Serie A, FIGC and the Italian Ministry of Environment, and will begin with the club’s home fixture against Cagliari on Saturday 19 September at 15:00 CET.

Launched by UEFA and European Leagues in June 2026, the Football Event Sustainability Manual provides clubs, leagues and national associations with practical guidance to embed environmental and social responsibility across the full lifecycle of football events, from planning and implementation to post-event evaluation. Udinese will be the first club to use the Manual as the framework for a dedicated league match.

Wider Sports News.title: NFL commissioner Goodell says league could restructure media deals to attract streamers
Wider Sports News.summary: American football league believes streaming services can improve accessibility and drive revenue growth despite possible political opposition. The post NFL commissioner Goodell says league could restructure media deals to attract streamers appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The National League Football (NFL) could restructure its media packages to reflect the rise of streaming platforms when it next goes to market. Commissioner Roger Goodell told CNBC that the league was considering adjusting its approach to reflect changing consumption habits in order to maximise both revenues and accessibility but would not be drawn on whether any changes would come into effect for the next cycle.

“One of the things we’re doing as a league is talking to our partners, talking to future partners, potential partners … and evaluating, should we repackage our current packages? Should we think differently about where we go with those things?” Goodell is quoted as saying.

Rugby.title: Olivia Apps: 'We rewatched the World Cup final
Rugby.summary: When Canada play England at Sandy Park this Saturday, it will be 357 days since the two teams met in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final.
Rugby.body:
When Canada play England at Sandy Park this Saturday, it will be 357 days since the two teams met in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final. It is a day that will live in the memory of rugby supporters for plenty of years, as 81,885 supporters piled in to Allianz Stadium to conclude the best-attended and most successful edition of the tournament ever.

While the memory is bright for many, for Canada, the memory carries a little more darkness. Beaten 33-13 in West London the side left the field knowing that they did not live up to the potential they had shown in the lead-up to the final.

Rugby.summary: Ireland hooker Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald admits she has found the smaller ball being trialled in women's rugby "challenging" in the build-up to Sunday's game against the United States.
Rugby.body:
Ireland hooker Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald admits she has found the smaller ball being trialled in women's rugby "challenging" in the build-up to Sunday's game against the United States.

World Rugby is trialling a size 4.5 ball - about 3% smaller than the size five used in the men's game, but the same weight - during September and October's WXV Global Series. England players May Campbell and Helena Rowland raised concerns before the Red Roses' win over Australia last week, while Wales wing Lisa Neumann spoke positively about the impact it has had on her passing.

Rugby.body:
Rugby Europe have announced the fixtures for this season’s Rugby Europe Super Cup, which will take place between October and December. The sixth edition will be played over five weekends in a round-robin format, beginning on October 10.

After three rounds of fixtures in October, the tournament will pause during the November Test match window before resuming in December. The Portuguese Lusitanos, Czechia’s Bohemia Rugby Warriors, the Netherlands’ Delta, Belgium’s Brussels Devils and Romania’s Romanian Wolves are all set for another season of high-intensity rugby as they battle for Super Cup glory.

Rugby.title: Rees-Zammit to return to wing for new season
Rugby.summary: Wales and Bristol back Louis Rees-Zammit says he will be a winger who can play full-back this season for club and country.
Rugby.body:
Wales and Bristol back Louis Rees-Zammit said he will be a winger who can play full-back this season for club and country, after spending much of the last campaign in the number 15 shirt.

Rees-Zammit returned to rugby last summer after almost two years away, as he tried to carve out a career in the NFL, and under Bristol boss Pat Lam and Wales head coach Steve Tandy was deployed at full-back consistently from the autumn, rather than his former position on the right wing.

Rugby.body:
Heather Fisher believes that Abi Burton’s brush with serious illness has pushed the back-row forward to new heights. Much like Fisher, Burton is a rugby sevens player now thriving in the 15-a-side game. In Burton’s case, we are only just getting to see what the 26-year-old can bring to the Red Roses on a regular basis.

The pair were once teammates when a teenage Burton first stepped into England Sevens camp and Fisher was at the tail-end of her playing career. Last weekend, the forward from West Yorkshire put in a Player of the Match performance in England’s 48-15 win against Australia in the WXV Global Series.

Much like Fisher, Burton is a rugby sevens player now thriving in the 15-a-side game. In Burton’s case, we are only just getting to see what the 26-year-old can bring to the Red Roses on a regular basis.

Rugby.summary: Exeter winger Campbell Ridl is set to miss much of the season after suffering a knee ligament injury.
Rugby.body:
Exeter winger Campbell Ridl is set to miss much of the season after suffering a knee ligament injury. Ridl had been one of the breakout stars of last season, scoring 17 tries in 24 games including one in Exeter's Prem final loss to Northampton Saints at Twickenham.

The 21-year-old, an England Under-20 player, was hurt in Exeter's opening pre-season game when they lost to Welsh side Scarlets earlier this month. It is the latest injury blow for Exeter, who will be without Italy lock Andrea Zambonin until November with a shoulder problem.

Rugby.body:
The bookmakers are unanimous: South Africa are the hot favourites to win the 2027 World Cup and achieve the unprecedented feat of three consecutive titles. It would take a bold punter to bet against them a year out from the tournament Down Under.

New Zealand gave it their best shot against South Africa in the riveting four-Test ‘Greatest Rivalry’ series but the Boks were too powerful, too organised and too experienced. This weekend, rugby’s newest competition Ultimate Sevens gets back underway in Biarritz, with the second round of action hitting the European mainland after it burst out of the blocks in Cardiff.

Rugby.title: 'Get the fear of your own tryline out of your heads'
Rugby.summary: Neil de Bruin never wanted to be a coach, yet is bringing radical ideas and fresh thinking to one of South Africa's biggest rugby beasts.
Rugby.body:
When Canan Moodie took a quick tap under his own posts, there was a visible jolt in the Bulls coaching box. They might have been 19 points up and cruising at home to Zebre, but there was a collective stiffening of spines, breath catching in throats as one of South Africa’s most exceptional talents called for the mark and set off at a gallop. While the coaches’ brows furrowed beneath their baseball caps, one man was punching the air.

Neil de Bruin is the team’s attack specialist. He’s been at Johan Ackermann’s right hand from Johannesburg to Osaka and back again. De Bruin is a free thinker; eager to innovate and wary of the formulaic patterns which can infect a rugby team. He is shaping the Bulls attack in ways which might seem radical to some of its traditional fanbase. Young, vibrant and knowledgeable, he delivers these messages with beguiling zeal.

Rugby.body:
TOKYO: Mason Flesch has become a backrow enforcer for Canada over 25 Tests, lining up as the fourth-most experienced starter in the side to face Fiji last weekend. But there was a time when Flesch didn’t play rugby at all, before finding it again as a teenager.

Flesch scored two tries against the Flying Fijians, who are the reigning Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup champions. The flanker led the way as Canada fought their way back more than once, producing a performance full of positives, despite falling to a 45-29 defeat.

Plus, we discuss his love of kicking and whether he’s going to become a long-distance kicker like Elliot Daly. We also hear about Ashy meeting the Queen, an awkward case of mistaken identity involving Dylan Hartley and Sir Jackie Stewart, and the most brutal pre-season fitness sessions.

Rugby.title: The numbers behind All Blacks' high ball struggles and the tactical change needed
Rugby.summary: The 2026 Greatest Rivalry Series was defined by the All Blacks inability to control the catch area. Knock ons became scrums, lost contests became second chance opportunities for South Africa.
Rugby.body:
The parallels between 2009 and 2026 are well documented for the All Blacks, with the high ball security becoming the dominant issue following three losses to South Africa. Much like 2009, the Springboks won 3-0 over the All Blacks with Fourie du Preez and both Steyns repeatedly putting up high balls. The wingers at the time, Joe Rokocoko and Sitiveni Sivivatu, two Fijian speedsters known for lethal running, couldn’t secure possession enough. The Boks fed off the resulting errors, that gave set piece and piggyback territorial wins.

It sounds like a familiar story with the All Blacks needing to find similar solutions to the Springboks kicking game. Rugby.title: Paul Williams: 'The All Blacks can still leave you spellbound like no other team'
Rugby.summary: The Boks may dominate the set-piece and lie top of the world rankings, but the All Blacks have shown they are on a redemption arc
Rugby.body:
Another month in rugby ticks by and it has only consolidated the fact in my head that the Boks’ scrum is the best we’ve ever seen, but the All Blacks shouldn’t give up hope, when in possession, they can still reach parts other sides cannot reach. Meanwhile, whisper it, but Australia may soon have the world’s best lock and closer to home, Lloyds’ sponsorship is a powerful shot in the arm for English rugby in these cash-strapped times.

Everyone has bad days. Regardless of career, we all have days when things don’t go quite to plan. But the difference between the All Blacks and normal people is that they rarely have two bad days in a row. In that regard, they are unique in rugby and perhaps even unique in sport. The lowest the All Blacks have been in the official world rankings is fifth (August 2022); prior to that, the lowest they had ever been was third – third is a dream for most rugby nations. This tour of South Africa has been further proof of their excellence. With what many would consider a rather average playing squad, given their history of individual brilliance, they have been the Springboks’ equals in a series of test matches that will live long in the memory. That does not mean they have matched the Boks in every aspect of play – they have not. The Boks’ scrum, for instance, has far outperformed the Kiwis’. But New Zealand have offset that disadvantage with ball handling so silky it would get the nod from even the most difficult to please of silkworms.

Rugby.title: Whitney Hansen shakes up Black Ferns side for Scotland clash
Rugby.summary: Whitney Hansen has made seven changes to the Black Ferns starting XV that beat France 28-14 last weekend.
Rugby.body:
Whitney Hansen has made seven changes to the Black Ferns starting XV that beat France 28-14 last weekend. This weekend, in their second WXV Global Series fixture, Alena Saili has been named at inside centre, where she partners Amy du Plessis. Sylvia Brunt drops to the bench.

Shyrah Tuliau-Tua’a is named on the wing and Tara Turner gets the nod at half-back. In the front-row, Maddison Robinson is named at loosehead and Mo’omo’oga Palu earns her second cap at tighthead prop. Layla Sae, who returned from an ACL injury after nine months, joins the back-row with Elinor-Plum King and Mia Anderson. Maama Mo’onia Vaipulu partners Laura Bayfield at lock.

Rugby.title: How Keira Bevan's positional change will give Wales 'another dimension'
Rugby.summary: Keira Bevan has spent much of her Wales career pulling the strings from scrum-half, but now, she has been handed the keys to the whole orchestra.
Rugby.body:
Keira Bevan has spent much of her Wales career pulling the strings from scrum-half, but now, she has been handed the keys to the whole orchestra. Head coach Sean Lynn has raised eyebrows by naming the experienced 83-cap international at fly-half, ahead of Wales’ WXV Global Series opener against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday 18 September.

And judging by what Wales have seen from her so far, Bevan is not simply filling a shirt. She is making the position her own. Her move was helped by an impressive end to the domestic season with Bristol Bears, where her performance against Gloucester Hartpury caught the eye of the Wales coaching staff.

Rugby.title: Leicester fly-half Searle agrees new contract
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers and England A fly-half Billy Searle signs a new contract with the Prem club.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers and England A fly-half Billy Searle has signed a new contract with the club. The 30-year-old joined Leicester in 2025 from French club Agen and scored 217 points in 24 appearances in all competitions during his debut season.

His form earned him a nomination for the Prem player of the season award in 2025-26. Head coach Geoff Parling told the club website:, external "Billy has produced performances of great attacking intent and game management, but what's impressed me the most is the professionalism he's shown and his intent to keep improving."

Rugby.title: Harry Potter actor makes surprise move to become part-owner of rugby team
Rugby.summary: Harry Potter actor Oliver Phelps has been named as part-owner of Ultimate Sevens team, Atlantic Novas.
Rugby.body:
Harry Potter actor Oliver Phelps has been named as part-owner of Ultimate Sevens team, Atlantic Novas. The 40-year-old, who starred as George Weasley in the blockbuster eight-film series, cited the “equal footing” for men’s and women’s players as a reason for his investment.

Last weekend, the brand-new competition headed up by former England and Great Britain captain Tom Mitchell launched in Cardiff. On the first weekend of Ultimate Sevens action, Clan Tartan won the men’s tournament and Phelps’ Atlantic Novas were winners in the women’s event.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: USA Women's Eagles
Rugby.summary: When Jack Hanratty took over as head coach for the USA prior to this year’s Pacific Four Series, it was clear that the Eagles were starting a journey firmly pointed towards Women’s Rugby World Cup 2033.
Rugby.body:
When Jack Hanratty took over as head coach for the USA Women’s Eagles prior to this year’s Pacific Four Series, it was clear that the Eagles were starting a journey firmly pointed towards Women’s Rugby World Cup 2033 on home soil.

Of course, there is a desire to build a strong squad to compete at the 2029 edition in Australia, but there is also a significant element of looking at the long game. With that in mind, you’d imagine Hanratty and his staff are reasonably happy to have secured two wins in his opening five matches so far this year.

Rugby.title: 'Liberated' Glen Young driven on by Rugby World Cup carrot
Rugby.summary: Having slipped down the national pecking order, there are now a slew of at least 10 locks jostling for Gregor Townsend’s attention.
Rugby.body:
Rugby World Cup 2027 may still be just over a year away, but its looming presence is already there in the bodies and minds of many a pro gearing up for the new season. The rested and freshly conditioned bodies, at least those not already carrying knocks, are somewhere approaching match-readiness as the United Rugby Championship and Gallagher PREM prepare for lift-off next week.

And despite the 12-month marathon to make it to the start line Down Under, minds are being sharpened by the prospect of participating in the next global rugby gathering. Edinburgh’s Glen Young is no different. It may be over two years since he won the last of his four Scotland caps – against Canada on his only Test start, before a torn pectoral muscle forced him home and a wretched season battling further injury hassles ensued.

Rugby.title: ‘Quins have under-performed... but with this set-up we can go on and do great things’
Rugby.summary: With Robbie Deans installed as performance director, flanker Jack Kenningham believes Harlequins can 'get back to where we should be'.
Rugby.body:
If there was a table for under-achievement in English rugby over the past four seasons, Harlequins would arguably top it. In terms of league finishes Newcastle are the failed state club, having propped up the rest for three of those seasons, but pre-Red Bull, the Falcons were operating on a budget so small it would no longer be allowed under the Prem’s salary floor policy.

Quins have enjoyed sufficient financial clout to spend up to the salary cap yet since the 2021 champions reached the play-offs the following season, they have finished no higher than sixth. The 2025-26 campaign’s last-but-one finish saw them fail to qualify for the Champions Cup for eight years.

Rugby.title: Revamped South African back line ready for WXV opener against Wales
Rugby.summary: The Springbok Women kick off their WXV Global Series campaign against Wales at Cardiff Arms Park this Friday 18 September.
Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women kick off their WXV Global Series campaign against Wales at Cardiff Arms Park this Friday 18 September. Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September, who were recently appointed as co-coaches, have revamped the backline and made one change to the pack that scored four tries against the Black Ferns in Johannesburg a couple of weeks ago.

The side will be captained by Babalwa Latsha, who her debut at Cardiff Arms Park in 2018, with Lindelwa Gwala and Sanelisiwe Charlie completing the front row. Vice-captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg, who scored a try in the Springbok Women’s last appearance at the same venue in 2021 and could extend her Test points record (221) in this match, gets the nod at 10, and will be joined by Felicia Jacobs in the half-back partnership.

Former England scrum-half Ben Youngs believes France must overcome South Africa in November if they are to remove what he sees as a growing psychological barrier against the world champions ahead of the 2027 World Cup.

The 127-cap England international was reflecting on Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry on his For the Love of Rugby podcast this week after the Springboks completed a 3-1 series victory over the All Blacks.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: South Africa
Rugby.summary: If the past 12 months have taught us anything, it's that if a game of rugby lasted only 40 minutes, the Springbok Women would be Women's Rugby World Cup contenders.
Rugby.body:
If the past 12 months have taught us anything, it’s that if a game of rugby lasted only 40 minutes, the Springbok Women would be Women’s Rugby World Cup contenders. At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, South Africa went into half-time level with the reigning champions, having matched New Zealand’s physicality and disrupted their attack. The Black Ferns eventually pulled away to win 46-17, but the Springbok Women had shown that the gap was narrowing.

At FNB Stadium two weekends ago, the pattern repeated itself. South Africa, again, produced a powerful, competitive first half before New Zealand’s greater attacking variety and ability to exploit space took control. The Black Ferns won 52-20.

Rugby.title: Wales make huge selection call for WXV opener against South Africa
Rugby.summary: Wales head coach Sean Lynn has made a huge selection call for his team's WXV Global Series opener against the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Wales head coach Sean Lynn has made a huge selection call for his team’s WXV Global Series opener against the Springbok Women. Keira Bevan has been named to start at fly-half against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. The 29-year-old, who is more regularly seen at scrum-half, will line up at half-back alongside Seren Lockwood. It is the first time that Bevan has started at fly-half for her country.

Lleucu George, who is Wales’ regular fly-half, is named among the replacements, where there is a 6-2 split. There are three potential debutants in the squad. Amy Williams has been named to start on the wing, while hooker Shanelle Williams and tighthead prop Elan Jones are on the bench.

Rugby.title: Carre and Keight win top Welsh rugby awards
Rugby.summary: Rhys Carre and Courtney Keight are given the top accolades by the Welsh Rugby Writers' Association.
Rugby.body:
Rhys Carre and Courtney Keight have been given the year's top accolades by the Welsh Rugby Writers' Association (WRWA). Saracens prop Carre and Sale centre Keight have been recognised with respective men's and women's player of the season awards after impressive performances during struggling campaigns for both national sides.

The WRWA men's list of honour features the likes of Sir Gareth Edwards, Barry John, JPR Williams, Phil Bennett, Jonathan Davies, Scott Gibbs, Ieuan Evans, Neil Jenkins, Rob Howley, Martyn Williams, Shane Williams, Leigh Halfpenny, Alun Wyn Jones, Aaron Wainwright and 2025 winner Jac Morgan.

Rugby.summary: Keira Bevan is to switch half-back roles after being selected to play at 10 for Wales' WXV opener against South Africa in Cardiff on Friday.
Rugby.body:
Keira Bevan will switch half-back roles after being selected to play at 10 for Wales' WXV opener against South Africa in Cardiff on Friday. The 29-year-old has been training at fly-half during pre-season and will partner Seren Lockwood.

Wales' regular 10, Lleucu George, is named among the replacements, while Kayleigh Powell is no longer an option having been ruled out of the campaign with a hamstring injury. Head coach Sean Lynn has included three uncapped players in his matchday squad, with Amy Williams named on the wing having impressed in a two-try display in June's uncapped Barbarians fixture.

Rugby.title: Rugby's Greatest Rivalry
Rugby.summary: Halfway through the series, Rassie Erasmus' Springboks mended their ailing areas of play and doubled down on their strengths. New Zealand could not respond.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks’ tour of South Africa has produced a series worthy of ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’. It has been full to the brim with drama and controversy on and off the pitch. Neither side can bear to mention the name of the other without a swear word muttered under the breath. And that is as it should be in the joust between the two greatest rugby nations on God’s green one.

What are the portents for South Africa and New Zealand on the final march towards a World Cup in Australia in just over 12 months? Has the tour influenced the future of the game for better or worse?

Rugby.summary: Las Leonas were close to landing an important win over Fijiana in round one of the WXV Global Series Challenger, but in the end the Pacific Island nation side managed a remarkable comeback to earn a 38-32 victory.
Rugby.body:
Las Leonas were close to landing an important win over Fijiana in round one of the WXV Global Series Challenger, but in the end the Pacific Island nation side managed a remarkable comeback to earn a 38-32 victory.

Despite the loss, the Spanish players felt they had made several strides since arriving in Hong Kong China, with the new attacking game plan looking promising and lethal. For captain and veteran lock Lourdes Alameda, the bitterness of the defeat shouldn’t blur the positive signs shown by the reigning champions of the former WXV 3.

Rugby.title: England winger Freeman signs new Northampton deal
Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints and England winger Tommy Freeman agrees a contract extension with the reigning Prem champions.
Rugby.body:
England winger Tommy Freeman has signed a new contract with Prem champions Northampton Saints, keeping him at Franklin's Gardens "for the foreseeable future". The 25-year-old made his Saints debut in 2019 and has gone on to make 118 appearances for the club across all competitions, scoring 79 tries.

He scored Saints' opening try in their 2024 Premiership final win over Bath and repeated the feat in their 2026 triumph over Exeter Chiefs. "Its a no-brainer in terms of the coaching staff we've got," Freeman told BBC Radio Northampton.

Rugby.title: Bristol fans can breathe a little easier over Kalaveti Ravouvou injury
Rugby.summary: News of Ravouvou's injury whilst playing for Fiji against Canada in the Pacific Nations Cup last weekend caused concern among Bears fans, who fear they could be in for another injury-hit campaign.
Rugby.body:
Kalaveti Ravouvou is only expected to be sidelined for three to four weeks with the leg injury that he picked up in Fiji’s 45-29 win over Canada in last weekend’s Pacific Nations Cup semi-final.

Ravouvou, one of the most destructive runners in the Gallagher PREM, started at inside-centre for the Fijians, partnering former Bristol centre Virimi Vakatawa. Playing with a heavily strapped left leg, the 28-year-old lasted 55 minutes, making just three carries, before being replaced by Tuidraki Samusamuvodre.

Rugby.title: What happens when the average person takes on a Red Roses preseason test?
Rugby.summary: As soon as I crossed the finish line, the only thing I wanted to do was lay on the ground. My lungs burned. It was impossible to escape the glare of the sun.
Rugby.body:
As soon as I crossed the finish line, the only thing I wanted to do was lay on the ground. My lungs burned. It was impossible to escape the glare of the sun. But I had finished.

Three weeks previously I received a text, out of the blue that read: “I have an idea for you… would involve you doing some running.” The idea was fairly simple; how would the average person, plucked from the street, fare doing a Red Roses fitness test?

Rugby.summary: Aoife Wafer and many of the Ireland Women’s team are heading into the WXV Global Series buoyed by Katie Taylor’s stunning finale at Croke Park.
Rugby.body:
Aoife Wafer and many of the Ireland Women’s team are heading into the WXV Global Series buoyed by Katie Taylor’s stunning finale at Croke Park. For every female athlete, young and old, across the country, seeing Taylor sell out 83,000 seats at Croker for her last ever boxing bout is beyond inspiring.

Rugby.summary: How has a drawn-out and public contract negotiation affected the relationship between Henry Pollock and Northampton Saints fans?
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock is determined not to blink first in his contractual face-off. Despite a deal with Northampton being close, amid reports of an agreement of about £400,000 a year,, external the back row stressed on Monday that his renewal was not signed.

Asked if he was looking forward to the end of the saga, stoked by Pollock's advisor Eddie Hearn, Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson joked that "it would have been good to have it sorted three weeks ago".

Rugby.title: KCB Rugby defends National Sevens Circuit title despite semi-final defeat
Rugby.summary: Kenya’s National Sevens Circuit competition has concluded for 2026, with KCB successfully defending their title despite falling in the semi-finals.
Rugby.body:
Kenya’s National Sevens Circuit competition has concluded for 2026, with KCB successfully defending their title despite falling in the semi-finals of the Christie Sevens in Nairobi over the weekend.

Coming into the final weekend, KCB held a valuable lead against arch rivals Kabras Sugar, who needed to both win the Christie Sevens and to also have KCB to finish lower than third to overtake them on the table and claim the crown.

Rugby.body:

She was introduced to the sport in Grade 12 at Langley’s D.W. Poppy Secondary, by teacher and coach Stuart Crowley.

Rugby.title: Wales hit by latest injury setback ahead of WXV opener
Rugby.summary: Kayleigh Powell has been ruled out of Wales' WXV Global Series campaign in the latest injury blow for Sean Lynn's side.
Rugby.body:
Kayleigh Powell has been ruled out of Wales’ WXV Global Series campaign in the latest injury blow for Sean Lynn’s side. The Harlequins back has sustained a hamstring injury that will see her miss Test matches against South Africa, USA Women’s Eagles and Japan in September and October.

Last week it was confirmed by the Welsh Rugby Union that Donna Rose, Kelsie Webster and Hanna Tudor had all been ruled out of action for the next two months. 27-year-old Powell started in all five of Wales’ 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations fixtures at full-back and scored one try as the team picked up a third wooden spoon in a row.

Rugby.summary: Wales have been dealt another injury blow ahead of their WXV Global Series with Kayleigh Powell ruled out of the entire campaign.
Rugby.body:
Wales have been dealt another injury blow before their WXV Global Series campaign with Harlequins' Kayleigh Powell ruled out of the entire tournament. The 27-year-old sevens Olympian was a standout player at full-back during the Six Nations and impressed at fly-half when Wales ended their nine match losing streak against the Barbarians in June.

But she will sit out Wales' Tests against South Africa, USA and Japan after suffering a hamstring injury in training. Powell wrote on her social media that she was "absolutely gutted" to be missing the campaign, but has "every faith that this team will do great things."

Rugby.title: Founder believes event can help give rugby sevens a much-needed boost
Rugby.summary: Founder believes event can help give rugby sevens a much-needed boost Hillingdon Times
Rugby.body:
The London City 7s founder believes the event can help give rugby sevens a much-needed commercial boost by bringing the sport into the heart of the City. Dan James sees a unique opportunity to unite top-level rugby, businesses and new audiences under one roof when the tournament returns to the Honourable Artillery Company on Thursday.

And for James, he wants the event to become a significant fixture for both the sporting and business calendars and sees the collaboration as central to growing the game. “Rugby, and rugby sevens in particular, has always had a problem with properly commercialising itself,” he explained. “What we’re trying to do is give it a really good foundation to grow into a really serious on-pitch product.

Rugby.title: Springboks report card: All 30 players rated in Rugby's Greatest Rivalry
Rugby.summary: South Africa emerged 3-1 winners over the All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, but it was far from a straightforward series for the world champions.
Rugby.body:
South Africa emerged 3-1 winners over the All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, but it was far from a straightforward series for the world champions. After falling 1-0 behind following an opening-Test defeat at Ellis Park, Rassie Erasmus admitted the All Blacks were in a “very good position”, with his side suddenly needing to win three matches in succession to claim the series outright.

But, as the Springboks have done so often before, they responded. Their scrum, maul and power game came to the fore as they ground out three consecutive victories to turn the series on its head.

Rugby.summary: A niche rugby record was broken in Lyon on the opening weekend of WXV Global Series 2026. New Zealand became the first side other than England to beat France on home soil since November 2018.
Rugby.body:
A niche rugby record was broken in Lyon on the opening weekend of WXV Global Series 2026. New Zealand became the first side other than England to beat France on home soil since November 2018.

That defeat nearly eight years ago – 14-0 in Toulon – was also at the hands of the Black Ferns. It means New Zealand and England are now the only sides to have beaten Les Bleues in France since Canada knocked them out of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2014 in Paris.

Rugby.title: Dafydd Jenkins reveals physical toll behind Exeter’s PREM final run
Rugby.summary: Dafydd Jenkins admits he played through the pain barrier to reach the Gallagher PREM final in June, but says a taste of the big stage has left him wanting more.
Rugby.body:
Dafydd Jenkins admits he played through the pain barrier to reach the Gallagher PREM final in June, but says a taste of the big stage has left him wanting more. The Wales lock scored his only try of the season in the 26-17 defeat to Northampton Saints in the Twickenham showpiece before undergoing an operation on a shoulder injury that he aggravated in South-West London.

Jenkins, who missed the Nations Championship, is now battling to be fit for the opening game of the PREM campaign against Gloucester at Sandy Park on Saturday week, and accepts injuries are part and parcel of the game.

Rugby.summary: Siya Kolisi and the Springboks veterans showed their class and durability as they push for an unprecedented third straight Rugby World Cup triumph.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks have come through the white-hot intensity of four Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tests with a 3-1 series victory as well as some important answers regarding their personnel.

Younger players such as Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morné van den Berg, Ethan Hooker and Cameron Hanekom passed the ultimate test against a resurgent All Blacks outfit, and as a result, all four should be in the mix when the squad departs for the World Cup in Australia next year.

Rugby.title: France call up two uncapped players ahead of Wallaroos clash
Rugby.summary: France head coach François Ratier has included two new uncapped players in his WXV Global Series squad.
Rugby.body:
France head coach François Ratier has included two new uncapped players in his WXV Global Series squad. Both Sana Lagrandeur and Marion Latonnelle have joined the squad ahead of this weekend’s meeting with the Wallaroos in Aix-en-Provence.

Lock forward, Lagrandeur, has been a regular feature for FC Grenoble Amazones since making her debut several seasons ago. It is her first-ever selection for the French national team, having never even been selected at age-grade level for her country.

Rugby.title: Canada dealt blow as star wing ruled out of European WXV tour
Rugby.summary: Canada have confirmed that Alysha Corrigan will miss the European leg of the team's WXV Global Series campaign with injury.
Rugby.body:
Canada have confirmed that Alysha Corrigan will miss the European leg of the team’s WXV Global Series campaign with injury. The wing has been a key performer for Kévin Rouet’s team in recent years. At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, the 29-year-old was a scorer of four tries as the team finished as runners-up.

Last season in JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby, as the Prince Edward Island native helped Saracens to a league title, she scored 11 tries. Corrigan also beat 48 defenders, completed 22 line breaks and assisted five tries.

Rugby.title: Two-time Super Rugby winner called into Fiji squad ahead of PNC Final
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks centre Seta Tamanivalu has been called into the Flying Fijians squad ahead of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 Final.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks centre Seta Tamanivalu has been called into the Flying Fijians squad ahead of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 Final, with Fiji Rugby confirming on Tuesday that Kalaveti Ravouvou had been ruled out due to injury.

Tamanivalu debuted for the Flying Fijians against Tonga in 2022, before also appearing in matches against Australia A in Samoa. The midfielder didn’t play international rugby for another three years after that, though, before returning during the 2025 edition of the PNC.

Rugby.summary: Former World Rugby Player of the Year nominee Joe Taufete’e returned to the international arena last weekend, coming off the bench for the USA.
Rugby.body:
Former World Rugby Player of the Year nominee Joe Taufete’e returned to the international arena last weekend, coming off the bench for the USA Eagles against Japan in Osaka. It was the front-rower’s first appearance in the Eagles’ red, white and blue jersey in more than 1,130 days.

Taufete’e was shortlisted for the most prestigious individual honour in men’s 15s rugby after the 2019 Rugby World Cup in Japan. The hooker made four appearances for the Eagles at the tournament, and was rewarded with a slice of unprecedented rugby history.

Rugby.title: The Chiefs' players are under the microscope for the All Blacks
Rugby.summary: While Savea is irreplaceable as a one-of-one player, it wasn't expected that the All Blacks would drop off so much in the final Test with the changes.
Rugby.body:
After losing captain Ardie Savea, centre Quinn Tupaea and openside Luke Jacobson to injury after the third Test, changes were expected for the fourth Test. While Savea is irreplaceable as a one-of-one player, it wasn’t expected that the All Blacks would drop off so much in the final Test with the changes.

There seems to be no progress with the high-ball issues, while an inability to recover from one error persists, with a cascade of errors contributing to massive momentum swings.

Rugby.title: Israel Dagg weighs in on All Blacks' ongoing high-ball struggles
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks' 43-28 loss, their third straight defeat against Rassie Erasmus' Springboks, highlighted several recurring issues.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks outside back Israel Dagg has pinpointed a couple of issues with the ongoing high-ball issues that have plagued Dave Rennie’s side, following their 3-1 series defeat against the Springboks.

The All Blacks’ 43-28 loss in Baltimore, their third straight defeat against Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks, highlighted several recurring issues. While the scrum improved during the fourth Test in Baltimore, the All Blacks’ lack of execution with ball in hand and discipline has continued to haunt Rennie’s side.

Rugby.summary: Sam Clarke is among a cohort of All Blacks Sevens players making a big impression in the 2026 NPC.
Rugby.body:
Sam Clarke is among a cohort of All Blacks Sevens players making a big impression in the 2026 NPC. Brothers Rob and Brady Rush helped Northland win the Ranfurly Shield for the first time since 1979. Sione Molia and Riley Williams traded tries in a recent Counties versus Wellington clash. Kele Lasaqa regularly plays for Bay of Plenty. Scott Gregory and Fletcher Morgan occupy spots in the Southland backline.

Clarke is running Taranaki’s backline at first five eighth. This role was thrust on him unexpectedly when Josh Jacomb was selected for the All Blacks tour of South Africa. “It’s my first time running a backline in a professional team. It’s been an awesome experience,” Clarke told RugbyPass.

Rugby.summary: The England star says he would consider playing abroad or changing sports altogether as part of an open-minded approach to his career.
Rugby.body:
England star Henry Pollock would consider playing abroad or changing sports altogether as part of an open-minded approach to his career. Pollock’s focus remains rugby and he is at the advanced stage of negotiations for a new contract with Gallagher Prem champions Northampton.

Rugby.title: O'Gara extends La Rochelle contract until 2031
Rugby.summary: La Rochelle head coach Ronan O'Gara signs a contract extension to keep him at the club until 2031.
Rugby.body:
La Rochelle head coach Ronan O'Gara has signed a contract extension to keep him at the club until 2031. O'Gara arrived at the club in 2019 after coaching spells with rival Top 14 side Racing 92 and New Zealand outfit Crusaders.

Following defeat in the 2021 European Champions Cup final, the former Ireland international signed an initial extension before guiding La Rochelle to back-to-back final wins in 2022 and 2023 - the club's first major silverware.

Rugby.title: Pollock still 'open to new opportunities' as Northampton talks continue
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock continues to play hardball in his negotiations over a Northampton Saints contract extension, insisting he is still open to offers from elsewhere.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock continues to play hardball in his negotiations over a Northampton Saints contract extension, insisting he is still open to offers from elsewhere, including overseas, and that he remains determined to be "quite selfish" over his future.

The 21-year-old England back row's current deal, thought to be worth about £150,000 a year, expires at the end of the forthcoming campaign. Pollock added Eddie Hearn to his advisory team earlier this year and the boxing impresario upped the ante by claiming his new client was "a seven-figure player", whose current pay shocked him.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly: Brilliant Boks and Six Nations Stateside?
Rugby.summary: Will the Six Nations stage a match in the USA? Can anyone stop South Africa?
Rugby.body: After South Africa crushed the All Blacks to seal a 3-1 victory in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, Ugo, Danny and Chris debate how you beat the Boks, and if anyone can stop them winning a record third successive World Cup. We react to your messages following our exclusive with Conor O’Shea and get Danny’s take on Steve Borthwick’s contract extension. Will we see a Six Nations match in the USA? World Rugby is keen, with the 2031 men’s and 2033 women’s World Cup heading Stateside, but would it actually help rugby break America, or would the tournament be selling its soul? We also discuss the new 4.5 size ball that is being trialled in WXV as the Red Roses come from behind to beat Australia.

Rugby.title: Rugby's Greatest Rivalry deep dive
Rugby.summary: New Zealand's scrum performance against a dominant Springboks pack fell well short of the standards set by titans of the past.
Rugby.body:
Twelve months ago almost to the day, New Zealand forwards coach Jason Ryan proclaimed a new era of All Blacks scrummaging. His charges had been caught napping at a late scrum in fortress Eden Park and had been pushed off their own feed at a brisk trot in the first match of a Rugby Championship double-header against the Springboks. On the morning after the ignominy, the last remaining member of Ian Foster’s 2023 World Cup coaching crew explained to the assembled Kiwi media that it was a one-off:

“We just want to get [the ball] out and play to be fair, but there’s one [scrum] where they climbed into us, we lost our footing, tried to get back up, and it was just too late. So that’ll be a ‘never again’ moment.”

Dames wing Kika Mulling scored four tries to start her WXV Global Series Challenger campaign on a high note. Both Gwen van der Schoot and Linde van der Velden registered a brace.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women ready to play the world's 'best' at WXV
Rugby.summary: The Springbok Women are relishing the opportunity to take on the world's best in the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women are relishing the opportunity to take on the world’s best in the WXV Global Series. On Friday night, South Africa start their autumn campaign against Wales at Cardiff Arms Park. In the weeks after, the Springbok Women will play Test matches against Italy, Spain and then a two-Test series against Ireland in Cape Town.

Coming into the WXV Global Series, South Africa have played plenty of rugby. In the summer alone, the side enjoyed two-Test series against the USA Women’s Eagles and Fiji, as well as a one-off clash with the Black Ferns as part of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry. They won three of those Tests and lost two.

Rugby.title: WXV Global Series 2026: Week 1 talking points
Rugby.summary: WXV Global Series 2026 started at the weekend with a trio of fixtures.
Rugby.body:
WXV Global Series 2026 started at the weekend with a trio of fixtures. Over the weekend we saw Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 champions England beat Australia 48-15, Canada were 64-26 winners over Scotland, and the Black Ferns registered a 28-14 win over France.

There were plenty of storylines wherever you looked. And it is only just the start. Everyone was a little stunned when the Red Roses went into half-time trailing the Wallaroos in Salford. Across the first half, Australia were by far the better team. Australia played with a physicality and intensity that we have rarely seen from the side before. It was thoroughly enjoyable stuff.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: Wales
Rugby.summary: Wales have everything to gain from this year’s WXV Global Series. After a false start in their Guinness Women’s Six Nations campaign, players, coaches and fans will be eagerly awaiting some positive results and a sign that the tide is turning.
Rugby.body:
Wales have everything to gain from this year’s WXV Global Series. After a false start in their Guinness Women’s Six Nations campaign, players, coaches and fans will be eagerly awaiting some positive results and a sign that the tide is turning.

It’ll likely be a nervous campaign. Since assuming the role in 2025, Head Coach Sean Lynn has been adamant that “changes are being made” in the Wales set up. But Lynn is fighting on two fronts. Not only trying to blood new young personnel into credible internationals but also find a rhythm that defines Wales’ playing style.

Rugby.title: English Champ breaks away from PREM and aligns with France
Rugby.summary: Champ Rugby has moved with the times and adopted the Top 14 try bonus system to reflect the growing trend of high-scoring matches.
Rugby.body:
Champ Rugby has moved with the times and adopted the Top 14 try bonus system to reflect the growing trend of high-scoring matches. While the Gallagher PREM continue to award try bonus points to teams scoring four tries whether they win or lose, the Elior Champ has decided to take a different stance ahead of Friday’s opening match of the season between Nottingham and newly-promoted Blackheath.

Now, only teams scoring three tries or more than their opponents will get rewarded. The losing bonus point system remains the same, though, with teams losing by seven points or fewer picking up an extra point.

Rugby.summary: The 33 French internationals who'll benefit from a new initiative designed to reduce their playing time during the club season have been named.
Rugby.body:
The 33 French internationals who’ll benefit from a new initiative designed to reduce their playing time during the club season, preventing exhaustion and keeping them in peak condition for the upcoming World Cup, have been named.

French outlet Midi Olympique revealed the list on Sunday, but the players and clubs concerned were already aware of the initiative, having been informed in advance by the Fédération Française de Rugby and the Ligue Nationale de Rugby.

Rugby.title: Women's rugby not to blame for region axe
Rugby.summary: The director of women's rugby at the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has hit back at "embarrassing" claims over why a men'e region is being axed.
Rugby.body:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has hit back at claims the women's programme is a financial drain on the men's game. WRU women's rugby director Nadine Griffiths said allegations she had read on social media that a region is to be cut because of investment in the women's game were "embarrassing".

And she added the women's game had in fact made money for the governing body. The Union has had a professional women's programme since the start of 2022 and there are now more than 40 contracted players.

Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has singled out Springboks duo Malcolm Marx and Cheslin Kolbe for being "head and shoulders above everyone" in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series, naming the hooker his player of the series.
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has singled out Springboks duo Malcolm Marx and Cheslin Kolbe for being “head and shoulders above everyone” in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, naming the hooker his player of the series.

The reigning World Rugby player of the year, Marx, featured in all four Tests, starting in three and coming on as a first-half substitute in the second Test. His work at the breakdown was decisive across the series, particularly in Cape Town, and he added a further two tries in the final two Tests, taking his tally to 29 in international rugby.

Rugby.title: Red Roses put Allianz Stadium date in the diary for 2027
Rugby.summary: England Rugby have confirmed that the Red Roses' 2027 Guinness Women's Six Nations finale against France will take place at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.body:
England Rugby have confirmed that the Red Roses’ 2027 Guinness Women’s Six Nations finale against France will take place at Allianz Stadium. The fixture will take place on Saturday 15 May and kick-off will be at 16:45. In the two teams’ past five meetings, an average of just over 60 points have been scored.

“Games against France are always a competitive battle and that’s what makes it one of the most enjoyable games to play in,” Meg Jones, England captain, said. “When you add the walk-in from the bus, the roar of the Allianz Stadium crowd and a sea of cowboy hats, it makes it an even more incredible occasion. It’s one we relish and are looking forward to.”

Rugby.title: Black Ferns call in potential debutant as Ruahei Demant cover
Rugby.summary: Ahead of their WXV Global Series fixture against Scotland, Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has called up uncapped first-five Arene Landon-Lane.
Rugby.body:
Ahead of their WXV Global Series fixture against Scotland, Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has called up uncapped first-five Arene Landon-Lane. Prior to New Zealand’s first game of the autumn against France, it was confirmed that the team’s co-captain Ruahei Demant had been ruled out of the European leg of their tour.

It meant that New Zealand were captained by Georgia Ponsonby in Lyon, while Hannah King was the starting fly-half in the 28-14 win against France. Demant sustained a calf injury in her team’s 52-20 win against the Springbok Women at FNB Stadium as part of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

Rugby.title: Baxter impressed with Exeter's opening cup victory
Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter was impressed with how his side dealt with "pressure moments" in their Prem Rugby Cup win over Bristol.
Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter says he was impressed with how his side dealt with "pressure moments" in their Prem Rugby Cup win over Bristol. The Chiefs, playing their first competitive game of the season, won 45-21 at Sandy Park on Saturday.

Olly Woodburn scored a hat-trick as Exeter led 17-0 in the first quarter before Bristol reduced the deficit to 10 points at the break. Kane James and Ethan Roots added tried early in the second half before Bristol hit back with an Ollie Harris try.

Rugby.title: Wales hopeful Megan Davey: 'The mindset is always that we're going to win'
Rugby.summary: Megan Davey wants to make the most of her Wales opportunity after a late call-up to Sean Lynn's WXV Global Series squad.
Rugby.body:
Wales hopeful Megan Davey does not believe that the team has a “losing mentality”. Ahead of WXV Global Series 2026, Wales have not won a Test match since July 2025. That victory in Australia against the Wallaroos is the sole victory Sean Lynn has had since his tenure as head coach began.

Ahead of their autumn block of fixtures, Wales dropped to 13th in the World Rugby rankings, a record low for the side since the rankings began. In June, Wales did beat the Barbarians 34-17 at Allianz Stadium. It is hoped that the result could help propel the team into home WXV Global Series fixtures against South Africa and the USA Women’s Eagles. The team will then travel to Japan for two Tests in October.

Rugby.title: Jordan Petaia returns as Les Kiss reshuffles Wallabies for Springboks
Rugby.summary: Reds outside-back Filipo Daugunu and prop Massimo De Lutiis both miss out due to workload management, while Dylan Pietsch is injured.
Rugby.body:
Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has made minimal changes to his squad for the Springboks in Perth on Sunday, September 27, drafting in three new players. Jordan Petaia, who hasn’t featured for the Wallabies since the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France, returns, alongside Force first-five Harry McLaughlin-Phillips and Queensland Reds prop Zane Nonggorr.

Petaia spent the 2026 season at French Top 14 club Perpignan, before signing with the Urayasu D-Rocks. Reds outside-back Filipo Daugunu and prop Massimo De Lutiis both miss out due to workload management, while Dylan Pietsch is injured.

Rugby.body:
Megan Davey's international ambitions have been reignited at her self-proclaimed 'old' age of 26. Loughborough Lightning's record appearance holder considered going into full-time teaching when she did not make Wales' 2026 Six Nations squad.

Her hopes were dashed again when omitted from Sean Lynn's extended training squad for the WXV Global Series. "There was a little bit of a wobble," admitted uncapped Davey. "It's hard to keep going when you're at my age, you feel old in the game."

Rugby.title: 'That sort of thing doesn't sit well with you': All Blacks coach left miffed by tackle on Josh Moorby
Rugby.summary: With the game in the balance in Baltimore with the All Blacks attempting to mount a comeback down 29-21, a try against the run of play to Kurt-Lee Arendse essentially killed off the contest.
Rugby.body:
With the game in the balance in Baltimore with the All Blacks attempting to mount a comeback down 29-21, a try against the run of play to Kurt-Lee Arendse essentially killed off the contest.

Fullback Damian McKenzie broke through the line and tried to link with winger Josh Moorby inside, only for the winger to drop the ball in the tackle of Cameron Hanekom. Arendse picked up the loose ball and run back 60 meters to score untouched through the tired defence of the All Black forwards.

Rugby.title: Whitney Hansen on Black Ferns facing life without 'influential' Ruahei Demant
Rugby.summary: But Hansen will have to prepare her side for another Test match without their inspirational skipper, Ruahei Demant, who continues to miss time with a calf injury.
Rugby.body:
Life as Black Ferns head coach has gone swimmingly to date for Whitney Hansen, who remains undefeated in the role after their 28-14 triumph over France in Lyon. Blues loose-forward Liana Mikaele-Tu’u starred for Hansen’s side, while Mererangi Paul, Mia Anderson, and Justine McGregor also crossed during the Black Ferns’ victory.

Hansen will have to prepare her side for yet another Test match without their inspirational skipper, Ruahei Demant, who continues to miss time with a calf injury. The experienced playmaker entered their historic encounter with the Springboks Women in Soweto last weekend, before picking up a calf injury that would rule the 31-year-old out of their WXV fixtures against France, Scotland, and England.

Rugby.summary: All Blacks assistant Neil Barnes believes that they are "seriously close" to the Springboks after a final 3-1 series result in the Greatest Rivalry Series in Baltimore.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant Neil Barnes believes that they are “seriously close” to the Springboks after a final 3-1 series result in the Greatest Rivalry Series in Baltimore. The Springboks lead 17-14 at half-time and had a 29-21 lead with 10 minutes remaining before a big decision on a tackle on Josh Moorby led to a try to Kurt-Lee Arendse.

South Africa secured the win with a 43-28 victory after a last minute try to Beauden Barrett reduced the final score. Speaking with Jason Pine in the aftermath, Barnes shared his thoughts on the final Test and the series.

Otago posted their highest score against Tasman in a 57-33 win on Friday night. Lucas Casey has scored a try in his last eight NPC games. In the Farah Palmer Cup, Waikato and former Black Ferns hooker Grace Houpapa-Barrett recently scored tries in 12 consecutive matches.

Rugby.summary: Mo'unga made his second appearance for the All Blacks since returning from a three-year deal in Japan at the Toshiba Brave Lupus.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes has weighed in on Richie Mo’unga’s first Test start since the 2023 Rugby World Cup Final, where the All Blacks were beaten 43-28 by the Springboks in Baltimore.

Rugby.title: Boks power & All Blacks of old
Rugby.summary: What did we learn from South Africa's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series victory over New Zealand?
Rugby.body:
South Africa further cemented themselves as the world's best team with a 3-1 victory over New Zealand in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series. After losing the opening Test in Johannesburg, the world champions won three straight games, comfortably claiming the series with a 43-28 win in Baltimore.

The fourth Test, played in the United States, came after three Tests in South Africa where the All Blacks continued to show promising signs under Dave Rennie. With the Rugby World Cup next year, what did we learn from the series, which replaced this year's Rugby Championship and will be played again in 2029?

Rugby.title: Gilmore: Better preparation behind Harlequins' 10/10 start to the season
Rugby.summary: Harlequins sit proudly at the top of Group B in the PREM Rugby Cup after bonus-point wins in their opening two fixtures.
Rugby.body:
Harlequins sit proudly at the top of Group B in the PREM Rugby Cup after bonus-point wins in their opening two fixtures. Having beaten Leicester 45-21 in their opening match, Harlequins returned to the Stoop a week later and bagged all five points again in a 29-14 comeback win against Northampton.

While the acid test will be the home game against Bath in the Gallagher PREM on 25 September, the London outfit appear to be in much better shape than 12 months ago. Danny Wilson’s abrupt departure to join the Wales coaching staff on the eve of the 2025/26 campaign left Harlequins without a head coach, and defence coach Jason Gilmore had to fill in at short notice.

Rugby.title: 'We can actually give it': The confidence Australia have taken from England loss
Rugby.summary: Wallaroos captain Siokapesi Palu stated that her team were "super-stoked" at full-time of their 48-15 loss to England in Salford.
Rugby.body:
Wallaroos captain Siokapesi Palu stated that her team were “super-stoked” at full-time of their 48-15 loss to England in Salford. At half-time of their WXV Global Series 2026 opener against the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2026 champions, it was Australia who led 10-5. It was the first time that the Red Roses had gone in at the break behind their opponents since 2020.

A Samantha Wood penalty and converted Faliki Pohiva try handed the Wallaroos a midway lead, with England’s sole effort coming from player of the match Abi Burton. Australia’s lead was also a result of their physicality. For the first 40 minutes, their more experienced pack made life tough in the loose and at the set-piece. It was a more than warranted lead.

Rugby.title: François Ratier's blunt two-word verdict after France's loss to the Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: François Ratier had a two-word response after his France team lost 28-14 to New Zealand's Black Ferns in their WXV Global Series opener.
Rugby.body:
François Ratier had a two-word response after his France team lost 28-14 to New Zealand’s Black Ferns in their WXV Global Series opener. In Lyon, the 54-year-old saw his team score tries through Pauline Bourdon Sansus and Line Queyroi, but succumb to tries scored by the Black Ferns’ Justine McGregor, Mia Anderson, Mererangi Paul and Liana Mikaele-Tu’u.

New Zealand were simply the better team from the first whistle to the last. France lost their own lineout six times and New Zealand had much the better of the scrum. In the midfield Hannah King and Maia Joseph marshalled the game superbly.

Rugby.title: Springboks achieve World Rankings record after wrapping up 3-1 series win
Rugby.summary: Having wrapped up a 3-1 victory in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series following their emphatic 43-28 win over the All Blacks in Baltimore on Saturday, South Africa have pulled further clear at the top of the rankings.
Rugby.body:
Having wrapped up a 3-1 victory in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series following their emphatic 43-28 win over the All Blacks in Baltimore on Saturday, South Africa have pulled further clear at the top of the World Rugby Rankings.

The Springboks held a 2.44-point lead over the All Blacks going into the series finale, but that has now increased to 3.95 points – the biggest it has been since July 2024. With more rankings points awarded for victories where the margin exceeds 15 points, South Africa’s lead would have been the highest it’s been for five years, since July 2021, had they not allowed All Blacks veteran Beauden Barrett to cross for a consolation try at the death.

Rugby.title: Title, ring and IVF eye opener
Rugby.summary: Wales forward Georgia Evans will not forget 2026 - having won a league title, got engaged, bought a house and started the process of having a family.
Rugby.body:
Wales forward Georgia Evans is smiling from ear to ear as she takes a seat in front of the media, and it is not surprising given the year she has had so far. While most of us were basking in record breaking temperatures, Evans began her summer by winning the Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) title with Saracens.

A few days later she was proposed to by England World Cup winner Hannah Botterman in front of a dreamy Greek sunset, and now boasts an engagement ring so big it should be classed as a structural hazard.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga doesn't hesitate when asked if these Boks are better than '23
Rugby.summary: Richie Mo'unga has labelled the 2026 Springboks a "complete team" after Rassie Erasmus' men claimed a thrilling Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series win in Baltimore.
Rugby.body:
Richie Mo’unga has labelled the 2026 Springboks a “complete team” after Rassie Erasmus’ men clinched a thrilling Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series win in Baltimore. The RGR trophy may have the ability to be split in two in the event of a drawn series, but those magnets will remain connected for the next four years and will sit next to four Rugby World Cups at South Africa Rugby HQ until the tour returns, on New Zealand soil, in 2030.

South Africa overcame a game-one loss at Ellis Park to claim three consecutive wins over their famous rivals, the All Blacks, including a decisive 43-28 win to seal a historic series win at M&T Bank Stadium on Saturday. While there were just three points separating the teams at halftime, the Boks struck first and second in the second half, claiming a commanding lead before the two nations traded tries in the final quarter.

Rugby.body:
Victorious Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus believes there was a clear turning point in Baltimore, where his side got the edge over the All Blacks. M&T Bank Stadium was packed to the rafters for the fourth Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, where the world number one Springboks powered past the All Blacks, 43-28.

That turning point would be the running game of exciting Springboks winger Kurt-Lee Arendse, who impressed with ball in hand during the second half in Baltimore. Arendse made several breaks for the Springboks, often forcing the All Blacks defenders to make tackles facing their own dead-ball line.

Rugby.title: South Africa cap series victory over NZ with Baltimore win
Rugby.summary: South Africa complete a 3-1 series win over New Zealand as the world champions' consistency, power and cohesion proves too much in the fourth Test in Baltimore.
Rugby.body:
South Africa completed a 3-1 series win over New Zealand as the world champions' consistency, power and cohesion once again proved too much in the fourth Test in Baltimore. After victory in the series opener in Johannesburg last month, the All Blacks jumped to the top of the world rankings and threatened to shake up rugby's world order.

However, South Africa clawed their way back to triumph - just as their director of rugby Rassie Erasmus had predicted. While New Zealand were spirited and skilful in pursuit of a win to square the series, the Springboks' go-forward up front and the depth of their bench kept the All Blacks at bay.

Rugby.title: 'Absolute joke' to be worried
Rugby.summary: England produce dominant second-half performance to comfortably defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
England produced a dominant second-half performance to defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series. The world champions, playing their first game since winning a record eighth successive Women's Six Nations title in May, were made to work for victory in Salford after trailing at half-time for the first time since 2020.

The Wallaroos led 10-5 at the break, with player of the match Abi Burton scoring England's only try in an error-strewn first half. John Mitchell's side responded emphatically after the interval, scoring seven tries to quickly put any prospect of a shock defeat to bed and extend their record winning run to 39 matches in front of a crowd of 9,251.

Rugby.summary: Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt has packed plenty into an illustrious career already.
Rugby.body:
Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt has packed plenty into an illustrious career already. The 37-year-old has earned 89 England caps to date, lifted multiple Guinness Women’s Six Nations titles, become a two-time Olympian by competing at the 2016 Rio Olympics and delayed Tokyo Olympics, and played big part in her club Gloucester Hartpury’s remarkable Premiership Women’s Rugby ‘three-peat’ success between 2022-2025.

Those achievements only scratch the surface of the renowned Red Roses scrum-half’s decorated career. Now, however, Hunt has her sights set on a new challenge – becoming part of history with the inaugural British & Irish Lions Women’s tour to New Zealand in 2027.

Rugby.title: Donnell eyes Irish call-up after Ulster move
Rugby.summary: New Ulster signing Ben Donnell says a motivating factor in his move to the province was the chance to force his way into the Ireland set-up and play international rugby.
Rugby.body:
New Ulster signing Ben Donnell said a motivating factor in his move to the province was the chance to force his way into the Ireland set-up and play international rugby. The 26-year-old is Irish-qualified through his Belfast-born father and as well as the chance to discover where his father grew up, he is aiming to catch Ireland head coach Andy Farrell's eye at his new club.

"My dad being from here, I wanted to see what Belfast was like and what it was like for him growing up here, but also I'm Irish-qualified and it gives me the chance to play international rugby," he told BBC Sport NI's Nicola McCarthy.

Rugby.summary: Talismanic captain Rachel Malcolm believes that Scotland lost their identity as a team between late last year and during the Guinness Women’s Six Nations in 2026.
Rugby.body:
Talismanic captain Rachel Malcolm believes that Scotland lost their identity as a team between late last year and during the Guinness Women’s Six Nations in 2026. She has also stated that shipping 267 points – including 41 tries – in five games as they finished a disappointing fifth in that Women’s Six Nations campaign “hurt” her soul given the importance the squad has placed on defence in recent years.

Now, with a busy period of WXV Global Series action getting underway this weekend, the 35-year-old Trailfinders Women’s back-row has vowed to help get the national team back up to the levels that they know they are capable of.

Rugby.title: 'It's been tough for Beauden': Dave Rennie explains All Blacks' No.10 switch
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie has shed light on the All Blacks' No.10 selection plan for the Greatest Rivalry tour after announcing a change at the position for the first time this year.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has shed light on the All Blacks‘ No.10 selection plan for the Greatest Rivalry tour after announcing a change at the position for the first time this year. The coach has turned to experience for the series decider in Baltimore, dropping Ruben Love in favour of Richie Mo’unga and bringing Beauden Barrett onto the bench.

Mo’unga served as All Blacks game-driver in a hotly contested midweek game against the Lions in Johannesburg three weeks ago, in what were his first minutes in the black jersey since the 2023 Rugby World Cup final, albeit a non-Test match. Having reclaimed his New Zealand eligibility after three years in Japan, the 32-year-old will now don the famous black No.10 shirt in the international arena for the first time in 1050 days.

Rugby.title: Finn Russell on his future: I won't make the same mistakes as the past
Rugby.summary: The mercurial fly-half has a couple of seasons left on his £1 million-year contract at Bath and will be 35 by the time the 2027 World Cup in Australia is over.
Rugby.body:
Scotland and Lions star Finn Russell doesn’t want to repeat the mistakes of the past and set parameters around the length of his Test career. The mercurial fly-half has a couple of seasons left on his £1 million-year contract at Bath and will be 35 by the time the 2027 World Cup in Australia is over.

By then, Russell will have certainly become a caps centurion for Scotland – he is five short of the milestone at present – and could have even overtaken Ross Ford (110 caps) as his country’s record holder for most Test appearances.

Rugby.body:
When Ed Spokes, the Harlequins head of recruitment, slid into Edward Sigauke’s DMs, the Zimbabwean hot rod thought the message might be a prank. He was midway through a Nations Cup campaign which took his international record to nine tries in 11 Tests, and burnished his credentials as one of the game’s most spectacular raw talents, but the idea of attracting Gallagher Prem interest still felt fanciful.

Two months later, the 22-year-old wing sits in a Guildford apartment; Quins kitbag in the corner of his room, play sheet on his laptop, and head somewhat spinning after a sense-scrambling move to Southwest London.

Rugby.body:
England prop Will Stuart will play his first game since rupturing his Achilles tendon when Bath take on Bedford tonight in a pre-season friendly at Goldington Road, which is being streamed by online broadcaster Clubber TV.

Stuart went off early in the second half of Bath’s Champions Cup victory against Munster in mid-December last year and missed the remainder of the 2025/26 season. But the tight-head, who committed his future to Bath in February by signing a new contract through to 2028, is now ready to return after a long period of rehabilitation and has been named on the bench.

Rugby.title: No plans for Ireland Six Nations game in US
Rugby.summary: There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says.
Rugby.body:
There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says. World Rugby's chief executive Alan Gilpin said on Wednesday that it would help any nation that wants to switch a Six Nations match to the US, as it continues its drive to spread the game stateside.

He used the example of Ireland v Italy as a game that would resonate with expatriate fans in the United States and could help the sport further establish itself there. But, in a statement issued on Friday, the IRFU dismissed the idea that it was considering moving any fixtures to the US.

Rugby.title: Prop Vunipola set to retire before Leicester move
Rugby.summary: Former England prop Mako Vunipola was planning to retire as a player before a phone call from from Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling changed his mind.
Rugby.body:
Former England prop Mako Vunipola says he was planning to retire before a phone call from from Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling changed his mind. The 35-year-old ex-Saracens front-rower, who won four Premiership titles and and the European Champions Cup three times with the London club, has moved back to England's top flight after two years in France with Vannes to play under former international team-mate Parling.

The pair featured for England together more than a decade ago and were also part of the British and Irish Lions team that toured Australia in 2013. Vunipola said it was "pretty random" how he was convinced to make a U-turn on his decision to hang up his boots and join a Leicester side that Parling guided to the Prem semi-finals in his first season at the helm.

If the All Blacks win this week’s concluding Test in Baltimore and level the series at 2-2, they will once again be rated as the best team in the world, a status that most Springboks would dispute, given they have won back-to-back Rugby World Cups.

Rugby.body:
Sporting history will be made one year from today when the first British and Irish Lions women's team runs out at Auckland's Go Media Stadium. They will be taking on six-time world champions New Zealand on 11 September 2027 in the first of a three-Test series.

Rugby.title: The Canada centre who experienced a Test debut week twice
Rugby.summary: Ince continued to reach even higher heights after being named to potentially debut in Canada’s Nations Cup opener against Spain.
Rugby.body:
Jacob Ince led the way as the Guelph Gryphons claimed a first-ever men’s national championship last November, and the midfielder was rewarded with a place in Canada’s squad for the all-new World Rugby Nations Cup in July.

“I had never actually played a professional game,” Ince said, having been given the chance to rub shoulders with Test veterans like Lucas Rumball and Ben LeSage. The 23-year-old then had the fairly rare experience of going through a debut Test week twice.

Rugby.summary: Codie Taylor will step back into the captaincy role against the Springboks at M&T Bank Stadium with a historic tour result on the line, after sitting out the third Test.
Rugby.body:
When All Blacks captain Ardie Savea left the field injured on Saturday at FNB Stadium, Luke Jacobson took over the captaincy duties only to also suffer a tour-ending injury. Also losing Quinn Tupaea in the Test left New Zealand with a significant hole in their leadership group heading into the decisive final Test in Baltimore.

It’s a leadership deficit that both supersub Wallace Sititi and head coach Dave Rennie have conceded will hurt the team, which faces a 2-1 series deficit after consecutive losses in Cape Town and Soweto.

Rugby.title: England captain Jones calls for fertility support
Rugby.summary: England captain Meg Jones wants the Red Roses to have access to fertility support and egg freezing.
Rugby.body:
Meg Jones, captain of the England women's rugby union team, wants Red Roses players to have access to fertility support and egg freezing. Speaking to BBC Sport, Jones said: "Why should my opportunity to have a family be taken away from me because I want to pursue my career?"

Jones revealed she has already started her fertility journey with her fiancee after visiting a clinic to have their egg count checked. The 29-year-old says that she's an "open book" on some subjects and wants to "share her journey" as she discusses both her upcoming wedding and family planning with equal comfort.
