Tennis.title: Six-time Grand Slam champion Salisbury retires
Tennis.summary: Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury retires from professional tennis.
Tennis.body:
Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury has retired from professional tennis. Londoner Salisbury chose this month's US Open as his final event and reached the semi-finals with his long-time partner Rajeev Ram, who had also decided to retire.

The venue was fitting, as in 2023 Salisbury and Ram became the first pair in history to win three consecutive US Open men's doubles titles. Salisbury is Britain's most successful men's doubles player of the Open era. He also won the 2020 Australian Open with Ram, and two mixed doubles titles with Desirae Krawczyk.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu reveals what her goals are for the coming years after withdrawing from the China Open
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu reveals what her goals are for the coming years after withdrawing from the China Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has endured a torrid year laden with injuries, and yet, on paper, it’s arguably been one of her most successful. After all, before suffering the stress fracture that has curtailed her entire summer, the Brit had reached finals in Romania and Queen’s, two tournaments supremely close to her heart.

Losing both of them will have hurt, but it marked great progress given her last final was the US Open in 2021. Emma Raducanu has been forced to miss both Wimbledon and the US Open because of this ongoing injury, with her return still undetermined.

Tennis.title: Kostyuk into Guadalajara last eight without playing a point
Tennis.summary: Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarter-finals of the Guadalajara Open even though the top seed is yet to play a point in the tournament.
Tennis.body:
Marta Kostyuk is through to the quarter-finals of the Guadalajara Open even though the top seed is yet to play a point in the tournament. The Ukrainian received a first-round bye in Mexico and got a walkover in her scheduled second-round match on Wednesday, when Taylor Townsend withdrew because of an illness.

Kostyuk, the world number 10, is now scheduled to get her tournament under way against the eighth-seeded Liudmila Samsonova of Russia, who edged Kayla Day 7-6 (7-4) 2-6 7-6 (7-5).

Tennis.title: Novak Djokovic to return to ATP's China Open on Sky Sports after 11-year absence from event
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic to return to ATP's China Open on Sky Sports after 11-year absence from event Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic has confirmed he will compete at the China Open this year, which runs from September 30-October 6 live on Sky Sports, marking a return to the event following an 11-year absence.

The 39-year-old recently dropped as low as No 12 in the world rankings following a shock first-round defeat to Argentina's Mariano Navone at the US Open. That defeat followed on from a third-round exit in May at the French Open - two underwhelming Grand Slam displays coming either side of a run to the semi-finals at Wimbledon, where he was well beaten in straight sets by eventual champion Jannik Sinner.

Tennis.title: Every player Jack Draper managed to beat in 2026 as he ends season early due to injury
Tennis.summary: Every player Jack Draper managed to beat in 2026 as he ends season early due to injury Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Still struggling with injuries, Jack Draper recently ended his 2026 season early. “Don’t usually love lots of words on here, but I wanted to update you that I am aiming to return to the tour at the start of 2027. Last summer, all the dedication and work I had put into this sport was coming together. It was all going my way, and the path seemed so clear. However, a complicated injury made things incredibly challenging, and since that moment I’ve been desperately trying to get back and feel as I once did on the court,” said Draper on Instagram.

“Managing so much change, adversity, and pain has helped me to grow massively in many areas of my life, but has also made me feel a level of fatigue that made it difficult to keep going. I am taking this time to reset and heal, so when I return, I am 100% ready to go.

Tennis.title: Charlotte to host WTA Finals from 2027
Tennis.summary: The WTA Finals will take place in the American city of Charlotte from 2027 on a three-year deal.
Tennis.body:
The American city of Charlotte in North Carolina has been chosen as the new home of the season-ending WTA Finals. The WTA says it wants to create the "Super Bowl of women's sports" and is hoping the three-year deal will bring more stability to an event that has had six hosts in seven years.

A planned 10-year stay in Shenzhen ended after just one year, with Guadalajara, Fort Worth, Cancun and Riyadh all taking turns since. Crowds have often been disappointing. "The WTA has always owned the WTA Finals, but now we are going to operate it, too," said WTA chair Valerie Camillo.

The 2026 season has easily been Jack Draper’s worst, and he’s now going to miss the rest of it. Don’t usually love lots of words on here but I wanted to update you that I am aiming to return to the tour at the start of 2027,” Draper wrote on Instagram.

Tennis.title: British tennis player Jack Draper to miss remainder of 2026 season amid ongoing arm injury - K-Jewel 99.3 FM
Tennis.summary: British tennis player Jack Draper to miss remainder of 2026 season amid ongoing arm injury K-Jewel 99.3 FM
Tennis.body:
British tennis player Jack Draper will miss the remainder of the 2026 season as he continues to deal with a persistent injury to his left arm. The 24-year-old former world No. 4 announced Tuesday that he plans to return to the ATP Tour at the start of 2027, ending a difficult campaign that has limited him to 15 matches and kept him out of all four Grand Slam tournaments.

Draper said on Instagram that the prolonged physical and emotional strain had left him fatigued and that he needed time away from competition. “I am taking this time to reset and heal so when I return I am 100% ready to go.” He said tennis remains his passion and that he hopes to return next year fully prepared to compete at the level he believes he can reach.

Tennis.title: More than the Score
Tennis.summary: It's been 23 years since an American last won a men's Grand Slam singles title
Tennis.body: Ben Shelton's defeat by Alexander Zverev in the US Open final means it's now been 23 years since an American last won a men's Grand Slam singles title. That didn't seem likely when Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi ruled men's tennis - but what does it really say about America's place in the tennis world? More than the Score's Delyth Lloyd talks to former professional player Denis Kudla, who's now a coach at Maryland's Junior Tennis Champions Centre - the place where US Open men's semi-finalist Frances Tiafoe and women's doubles finalist Robin Montgomery learned the game. He tells Delyth about his journey through the US developmental system, and how he built a 16-year career that saw him play at all four Grand Slams. He also shares the lessons he's now instilling in young players, and the importance of role models in their development. Delyth's also joined by Ben Rothenberg, editor of tennis magazine Bounces, who talks about why US women have had much more recent success at Grand Slams than their male counterparts - and why he believes a breakthrough on the men's side could happen very soon. Unexpected questions and beyond the scoresheet chat. More than the Score tells stories from all over the world of sport. From Formula One to netball, MMA to figure skating, and Grand Slam tennis to Diamond League athletics. We've got interviews with extraordinary athletes, as well as the experts working behind the scenes, from football super-agents to the coaches keeping athletes in peak form. Plus, we've got the expertise of the BBC's top journalists, who share their insights from decades of covering sport at all levels. Tennis.title: Jack Draper Announces He Will Miss the Rest of the Tennis Season
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper Announces He Will Miss the Rest of the Tennis Season Town & Country Magazine
Tennis.body:
After dealing with a series of injuries since last year’s Wimbledon, British tennis player Jack Draper announced he will miss the rest of the season. “Don’t usually love lots of words on here but I wanted to update you that I am aiming to return to the tour at the start of 2027. Last summer all the dedication and work I had put into this sport was coming together. It was all going my way and the path seemed so clear. However a complicated injury made things incredibly challenging and since that moment I’ve been desperately trying to get back and feel as I once did on the court,” he wrote.

Draper continued, “Managing so much change, adversity and pain has helped me to grow massively in many areas of my life but has also made me feel a level of fatigue that made it difficult to keep going. I am taking this time to reset and heal so when I return I am 100% ready to go.” He has been managing a chronic elbow injury in his left arm and a right knee injury.

Tennis.title: Draper decides not to play again this season
Tennis.summary: Former world number four Jack Draper will not play again this season, but says he is aiming to return to the tour at the start of next year.
Tennis.body:
Former world number four Jack Draper will not play again this season, but says he is aiming to return to the tour at the start of next year. The 24-year-old has been suffering with bone bruising in his serving arm and has only played nine events since last year's Wimbledon.

Draper missed the US Open, after losing in the first round in Montreal and Cincinnati last month - and was in tears during his defeat to France's Terence Atmane in Canada. "I am taking this time to reset and heal so when I return I am 100% ready to go," Draper posted on Instagram., external

Tennis.title: Jack Draper ends season early due to injury, targeting 2027 return to ATP Tour
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper ends season early due to injury, targeting 2027 return to ATP Tour The New York Times
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has said he will not play again in 2026 due to fatigue from a “complicated” injury and is targeting a return to the ATP Tour at the start of 2027. The 24-year-old Briton, ranked No. 155 in the world, announced the decision on Instagram on Tuesday after being limited to 15 competitive singles matches this season by a chronic elbow injury in his left, playing arm and a separate right knee injury.

The former world No. 4 first experienced pain in his left elbow during the 2025 clay-court season and later developed serious bone bruising which forced him to withdraw from the U.S. Open after his first-round victory. He returned for Great Britain in the Davis Cup in February before making his ATP Tour comeback in Dubai later that month.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu’s former coach issues defence of Alexander Zverev and insists he plays within the rules
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu’s former coach issues defence of Alexander Zverev and insists he plays within the rules Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev may have just won the US Open title, but the reaction has been far from overwhelmingly positive. After all, one negative narrative that really picked up as he went through the competition surrounded his serve, and particularly how long it took him to toss the ball.

It was stated that he had bounced the ball roughly 12,000 times before the semi-final, and during the final, the umpire had to warn him for taking too long between serves. Ben Shelton has discussed this controversy surrounding Zverev already following his loss, whilst others have called for a rule change because of it.

Tennis.title: From Challenger Tour to Davis Cup
Tennis.summary: Briton Toby Samuel is to make his Davis Cup debut for Great Britain after what he calls a "surreal" 12 months.
Tennis.body:
Toby Samuel says it was "one of the best moments in my life" when he was selected in Great Britain's Davis Cup team to face Ecuador this weekend after a breakthrough year. The 23-year-old was handed his maiden Davis Cup call-up after a rapid rise over the past 12 months, climbing into the top 100 in the world rankings and making his debut in three Grand Slams.

"It's surreal being in this position now from where I was eight, nine months ago, [when I was] hopefully trying to play some Challengers, and now I'm sat here ready to play the Davis Cup - it's crazy," he told BBC Points West.

Tennis.title: How far Emma Raducanu has fallen in the WTA rankings after not playing in the US Open
Tennis.summary: How far Emma Raducanu has fallen in the WTA rankings after not playing in the US Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has suffered another setback amid her current injury absence. Raducanu won the US Open in 2021, but on the five-year anniversary of her famous victory, she was unable to compete at the New York major.

This came as a result of a stress fracture Raducanu suffered in her right lower leg during the grass court season, which also forced her to withdraw from Wimbledon. With Raducanu unable to earn any ranking points at the US Open this year, she has now suffered a significant drop in the latest update.

Tennis.title: When will Raducanu return to tennis and what is her upcoming schedule?
Tennis.summary: When will Raducanu return to tennis and what is her upcoming schedule? TNT Sports
Tennis.body:
The summer of 2026 looked as though it could be a bright one for Emma Raducanu when she made the final of Queen's, having played some of her best tennis since her shock US Open win in 2021, but she has been absent on tour since.

Raducanu was beaten in the final by Donna Vekic but said it had been an "incredibly special" week that "deserves to be celebrated". Unfortunately for Raducanu, she has not been on court since, pulling out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament due to a lower leg stress fracture.

Tennis.title: Episode 2: There's always a contender
Tennis.summary: There’s a new number one - but not everything is easy when you’re at the top.
Tennis.body: Steffi Graf had been world number one for 3 years; it seemed like nobody could challenge her supremacy. But then along came a teenage girl from Yugoslavia, whose aggressive style - that came with grunting to match - challenged Graf’s dominance as well as the status quo. Finally, there was a contender. Clare Balding takes us through the most exciting moments in this emerging rivalry, as well as the darkness that swirled behind the scenes. How Seles’ record breaking was sidelined for her breaking of etiquette, and what it was like for young girls like her who found themselves in the very adult world of elite tennis in the 90s. In the age of the indomitable Steffi Graf, what made people think that Seles could be the greatest player the women’s game had ever seen? And what put both players on a collision course that would end with one of them in hospital? Tennis.title: Zverev turns US Open tears into triumph
Tennis.summary: How a more composed Alexander Zverev stayed 'zen-like' to beat Ben Shelton and win the US Open, six years after a heart-breaking defeat in the final.
Tennis.body:
As he stepped up to the baseline, Alexander Zverev could be forgiven for letting his mind slip back to the last time he served for the US Open title. Six years ago, the German top seed threw away a two-set lead in a devastating loss to Dominic Thiem, having served for the match in the fifth set.

This time, instead of his own nerves, it was American Ben Shelton and the majority of the 24,000-strong crowd that stood in Zverev's way. But this was a different Zverev: a Grand Slam champion now, having won the French Open in June.

Tennis.title: Zverev caps transformational year with US Open triumph
Tennis.summary: Alexander Zverev lands his second Grand Slam title after ending Ben Shelton's hopes of becoming a rare home US Open men's champion.
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev used his greater experience to beat home hope Ben Shelton in the US Open final and quiet a partisan crowd hoping to laud a rare American men's champion. German top seed Zverev lifted a heavy burden by winning his first major title at this year's French Open and has quickly added another with a 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 victory over Shelton in New York.

At the start of the season, there were question marks over whether 29-year-old Zverev would ever win one of the sport's most prestigious prizes. Now he is celebrating becoming a multiple Grand Slam singles champion, having seen the path to glory partially cleared by injuries to Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz.

Aryna Sabalenka cut a forlorn figure as she sat staring into space following a painful defeat by Elena Rybakina in the US Open final. As Rybakina celebrated her third Grand Slam title following a 6-4 5-7 6-2 win in New York, cameras pictured Sabalenka deep in thought as she sat in silence with her team.

At a tournament which has delivered so much success for two-time champion Sabalenka, the disappointment the 28-year-old has faced in the past week leaves her with plenty to ponder.

Tennis.title: From struggling to walk to lifting trophy
Tennis.summary: Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one.
Tennis.body:
Elena Rybakina arrived in New York unable to walk without pain after injuring her foot. She leaves the city as the US Open champion and new world number one. Kazakhstan's Rybakina produced a brilliant performance to beat two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2 in Saturday's final and repeat her Australian Open success against the same player in January.

Clutching the trophy on Saturday night, Rybakina reflected that "some magic is happening" for her after her difficult lead-in to the tournament. The 27-year-old aggravated a foot injury during her quarter-final in Cincinnati against Iga Swiatek last month, a little over a week before the final major of the year began.

Tennis.title: Only Roland Garros towel left
Tennis.summary: Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.
Tennis.body:
Ukrainian tennis player Dayana Yastremska has said her family's flat has been destroyed in a Russian aerial strike on the Black Sea port of Odesa. "This is what the 'Russian world' looks like. A direct hit by a Kalibr cruise missile," she wrote on social media, showing a photo of a burning multi-storey residential building.

"The only thing that survived was a Roland Garros... towel," the 26-year-old added, posting an image of a famous clay orange towel from Paris's Grand Slam tournament hanging from the wreckage.

There was double success for Britain at the US Open on Saturday, with Alfie Hewett regaining his wheelchair singles title and Neal Skupski finally claiming the men’s doubles crown.

Emotional Hewett burst into tears after beating Tokito Oda 6-0 7-6 (7-5) to deny the 20-year-old Japanese star a calendar Grand Slam. The 28-year-old, who was beaten by Oda in the finals of the French Open and Wimbledon this year, said: "It's taken lot of hard work, a lot of soul-searching at times, a lot of reflecting.

Tennis.summary: Great Britain's Alfie Hewett beats Japanese top seed Tokito Oda to win a fifth US Open title and his 11th Grand Slam singles crown overall.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Alfie Hewett beat Tokito Oda to clinch a fifth US Open men's wheelchair singles title and prevent the Japanese top seed from completing a clean sweep at the Grand Slams in 2026.

A 6-0 7-6 (7-5) victory meant Hewett added to the doubles title he won alongside fellow Briton Gordon Reid on Friday. Hewett, 28, lost to Oda in the finals of the French Open and Wimbledon earlier this year, winning only two games in a 6-1 6-1 defeat at SW19, while the Japanese also triumphed at January's Australian Open.

Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison won the US Open men's doubles title to claim their second Grand Slam trophy together. The fifth seeds did not drop a set in New York as they beat sixth seeds Tim Puetz and Kevin Krawietz 6-4 7-6 (8-6) to secure the title.

Victory adds to Skupski and Harrison's Australian Open triumph in January in what was their first Grand Slam as a pairing. Skupski had suffered a heartbreaking defeat in last year's US Open final, missing three championship points when he reached the showpiece alongside fellow Briton Joe Salisbury.

Tennis.title: Could Jack Draper Follow the Path of Robin Soderling?
Tennis.summary: Could Jack Draper Follow the Path of Robin Soderling? sports.yahoo.com
Tennis.body:
- Could Jack Draper Follow the Path of Robin Soderling? The summer of 2011 should have been Robin Soderling's. He was ranked No. 4 in the world, had reached consecutive French Open finals, and had beaten Rafael Nadal at Roland Garros in 2009, the only player to do so on clay before 2015. He was 26 years old and playing some of the best tennis of his life. Then, in July, he felt something was wrong. He played on anyway.

He won the Swedish Open in Bastad, which turned out to be the last professional match he would ever play. Shortly after, he was diagnosed with mononucleosis, the viral infection that had been draining him for weeks. He tried to come back for four years. He never did.

In the days before the 2021 US Open, Tim Henman made a transatlantic call to an old friend. Andrew “Flex” Richardson, a former touring pro of the same vintage, had been the best man at Henman’s wedding.

Despite his towering 6ft 7in frame, Richardson is a low-key, publicity-shy character. And yet, only a couple of months earlier, he had taken on a very high-profile post: Emma Raducanu’s coach.

Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka has lost the world number one ranking to Elena Rybakina - but has the chance to take revenge in the US Open final.

And as the pair prepare to meet in Saturday's final, Sabalenka knows her 99-week stay at the top of the world rankings is at an end.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina is assured of replacing Sabalenka at the top of the rankings, guaranteeing that by reaching the semi-finals. Having also beaten the Belarusian to win this year's Australian Open title, Rybakina now has the opportunity to inflict further damage.

Tennis.title: US Open: Ben Shelton takes down Frances Tiafoe to seal Alexander Zverev showdown in final on Sunday in New York
Tennis.summary: US Open: Ben Shelton takes down Frances Tiafoe to seal Alexander Zverev showdown in final on Sunday in New York Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Ben Shelton defeated compatriot Frances Tiafoe in an electric US Open semi-final on Friday to secure a title showdown with Alexander Zverev. On a poignant evening that began with commemorations marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, Shelton came from a set down to beat Tiafoe 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5 and move closer to ending a 23-year American wait for a men's singles Grand Slam champion.

No home male player has won a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick triumphed in Flushing Meadows in 2003. Shelton will now have a chance to claim his maiden Grand Slam crown.

Tennis.title: Hewett and Reid secure sixth US Open doubles title
Tennis.summary: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid come from a set and a break down to win the men's wheelchair doubles title for the sixth time at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid came from a set and a break down to win the men's wheelchair doubles title for the sixth time as a partnership at the US Open. Five years on from their most recent title at Flushing Meadows, the legendary pair battled back to beat Spain's Martin de la Puente and Ruben Spaargaren of the Netherlands 2-6 6-3 10-7 in a match tie-break.

It is a remarkable 30th Grand Slam doubles title for 34-year-old Reid, 11 years on from the Scot's first, with 26 of them coming alongside Hewett. "We've not won here for five years so this is something we've been desperate for and highly motivated for," Hewett, 28, said.
Tennis.copy:

Tennis.summary: On Friday, the US Open will pause and remember the victims of the 9/11 terror attack that took place 25 years ago.
Tennis.body:
The Arthur Ashe Stadium will glow light blue from dusk until dawn as the US Open marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. American flags will be flown at half-mast as New York remembers the 2,977 people who died when hijackers crashed passenger jets into the Twin Towers in Manhattan on that day in 2001.

That year's US Open had concluded just two days earlier, with Lleyton Hewitt winning the men's singles title. American player James Blake had lost in the second round that year and was in Augusta, Georgia, on Tuesday, 11 September.

Tennis.body:
US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027. Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule.

It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages.

Tennis.body: Today the city of New York marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks which saw two hijacked passenger jets flown into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Centre. The US Open of 2001 had finished two days prior to the attacks with Venus Williams and Leyton Hewitt winning the singles titles. Russell Fuller has been speaking to James Blake - a former top 5 player - who was born in New York and played in the 2001 edition of the tournament about how sport played a role in America's healing process and how life changed for those who lived in the city in the wake of the atrocity.

Golf.title: FlightScope's Mevo Gen2 is everything you'd want in a personal launch monitor
Golf.summary: The new FlightScope Mevo Gen2 cuts the price of the previous version nearly in half while also offering impressive accuracy. The post FlightScope’s Mevo Gen2 is everything you’d want in a personal launch monitor appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The personal launch monitor (PLM) category continues to be one of the most innovative in golf. New options come out all the time, so it’s often about picking the option that suits your needs the best.

You can chose between going with something more focused as a game to create a simulator or something more focused on being used on the range for practice and instruction. Your use might also impact how much you’re willing to spend. If you’re just looking for something to make a game in your basement or give simple feedback on the range, then you might spend something in the $500-$700 range. Looking for more advanced data and accuracy that can keep up with the Trackmans and Quad Maxs of the world? Then you’re looking at spending somewhere between $3,000-$5,000.

Golf.title: Pebble Beach course change draws scorn. But critics didn’t have full story
Golf.summary: Justin Thomas was among critics of Pebble Beach’s decision to remove a tree on the 16th hole. But the resort says it had little choice. The post Pebble Beach course change draws scorn. But critics didn’t have full story appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Justin Thomas is not the Lorax but he speaks for the trees. He thinks golf courses cut down too many of them. Thomas said as much this week in a social-media post, citing a hole on a famous course to underscore his point: the par-4 16th at Pebble Beach Golf Links.

At 400 yards from the tips, the hole plays gently downhill from the tee, followed by an approach over a gully and between goal posts of Monterey cypress trees. At least, it used to. In early September, Pebble Beach removed the tree on the right, which stood some 90 yards short of the green.

Golf.title: At this year's Bridges Cup, the pressure comes with 1 unanswered question
Golf.summary: The Bridges Cup, a premier mid-amateur team match-play competition, heads to Trump Turnberry with even more pressure and storylines to play out. The post At this year’s Bridges Cup, the pressure comes with 1 unanswered question appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
You can call it a friendly rivalry between Jeff Fujimoto and Simon Holt, the two captains at next month’s Bridges Cup. They agree on most things, like the fact they are thrilled the premier mid-amateur international team match-play competition is heading to a venue as prestigious as Trump Turnberry. And that the Bridges Cup, about to get underway for the fourth time, is instrumental in promoting mid-amateur golf and showcasing the players who balance work and family while still competing at a high level.

The only thing Fujimoto and Holt can’t agree on? Which team should be favored in the upcoming Bridges Cup. “The level of competition every year seems to get stronger and stronger,” said Fujimoto, the U.S. captain. “It’s exciting — I think we are going to go in and upset them.”

Golf.body:
After Ryan Gerard wrapped up a third-place finish at the Tour Championship — the big-money season finale in which he beat every U.S. Presidents Cup team member not named Scottie Scheffler — he was asked where he was headed to begin his offseason. “I’m going to get on a red-eye here in a couple hours to play DP World Tour next week,” he said. “We’re getting ready to grind. Season’s not over for me. Frustrated with some of the results, a lot of positives, but still work left to do.”

DeChambeau went from misunderstood mad scientist to crowd favorite by the time he won the 2024 US Open, thanks to a new fan-first attitude and a successful move into YouTube golf.

The American is now one of the biggest names in YouTube golf with his quirky content and while he's not challenged in Majors recently he's continued to win LIV Golf events. And Norman, the architect behind LIV's launch, believes that DeChambeau could not have achieved all this success without the team-based tour behind him.

Golf.title: New DPWT schedule will force fascinating Ryder Cup decision
Golf.summary: The DP World Tour's new schedule features several fascinating changes — including the Irish Open, national opens and Ryder Cup strategy. The post New DPWT schedule will force fascinating Ryder Cup decision appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour released its 2027 schedule on Wednesday — and it featured a few notable changes. There are some big-time additions. The Singapore Open (in April, now presented by Deutsche Bank) and the Hong Kong Open (in October) will be co-sanctioned with the Asian Tour. LIV Golf had played events in both places several times in recent years; their realignment with the DP World Tour is a story in and of itself.

The Open de Portugal (in May) also returns to the schedule for the first time since 2020 and adds to the DP World Tour’s roster of historic national opens. Those national opens have been a major focus of the tour as it seeks to double down on the significance and meaning of its global calendar. (The DPWT has been referring to itself as “Golf’s Global Tour,” including in this new schedule release.)

Golf.title: Why the winningest golf ball on the 2026 PGA Tour is 7 years old
Golf.summary: Titleist, to the surprise of no one, dominated the winning golf ball counts in 2026, but it was a ball from 2019 that actually led the way. The post Why the winningest golf ball on the 2026 PGA Tour is 7 years old appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
No one should be surprised that Titleist again led the counts for the PGA Tour’s winningest golf balls this year. The company counted 26 victories during the 2026 FedEx Cup season, more than all the other brands combined and more than six times as the second-place brand. All of those victories were recorded by variants of the flagship Pro V1 and Pro V1x golf balls.

But what’s really interesting and unique about Titleist is that many Titleist golf ball users are playing an older model that Titleist continues to manufacture for them. That’s not because they feel like the new model isn’t better, it’s just different enough that they prefer to stick with what’s comfortable.

Golf.title: AI golf commentator weathers harsh reviews. Its creator responds
Golf.summary: The reviews are in for AI golf analyst Duff Foreman, and they have not been kind. One of Duff’s creators weighs in on the bot's debut. The post AI golf commentator weathers harsh reviews. Its creator responds appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Among the many understandable reasons to fear the rise of AI — security threats, wealth concentration, existential risk — the emergence of golf’s first autonomous tournament commentator probably should rank low on the list of concerns. Still, in pockets of the golf world, the introduction of just such a chatterbot has stirred up agita and scorn. A sampling of golf-observer commentary from the complaint box known as X:

The lamest broadcasters in golf can rest easy, AI slop has made their job is safe. How about we f—ing send this straight into space with a one way ticket. The teeth-gnashing and eye-rolling began last week when Troon Golf distributed a press release about the 2026 New Mexico Open, slated for Sept. 14-16 at Turtleback Mountain Golf & Resort in Elephant Butte, about two hours south of Albuquerque. The event, which is run by the Sun Country Section of the PGA of America, has three former PGA Tour winners in the field, Notah Begay III, Matt Every and Sean O’Hair, but drew buzz not for who would be on the course but in the booth: Ryan Burr, who you might know from Golf Channel, alongside Begay, who would be Ping-Ponging between playing and commentating, and — the real attention-grabber — a new-to-the-scene broadcaster named Duff Foreman.

Golf.title: Woods seen on range for first time since car crash
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago.
Golf.body:
Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago. The 15-time major champion was seen hitting balls at Liberty National in New Jersey in a video shared on his Instagram, external before the Nexus Cup, a charity event he is hosting to raise funds for his TGR Foundation.

Woods, 50, also held a clinic where he was asked by the master of ceremonies about his game and replied: "I can hit pretty much anything." It comes six months after the golfer rolled his Land Rover in Florida and had to crawl out of the passenger door of the car. He refused a urine test.

Golf.body:
Brian Rolapp says he’s been keeping up with current events. But any news the PGA Tour’s CEO had regarding a potential accelerated return of LIV Golf players to his tour was only old news.

In announcing details of a new format coming to the PGA Tour in 2028, Rolapp said Tuesday that the PGA Tour would not re-introduce its “Returning Member Program” to bring back one-time Tour pros who had joined LIV. Rolapp had also said that last month at the Tour Championship, but in the weeks since, LIV has filed for bankruptcy, leading to speculation that its players may be seeking to leave.

Golf.title: PGA Tour says no to shortcut for LIV Golf stars like Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau to return
Golf.summary: PGA Tour says no to shortcut for LIV Golf stars like Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau to return usatoday.com
Golf.body:
The PGA Tour's CEO said the tour is not considering another returning member program for former LIV Golf players, reinforcing the likelihood that stars Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm won't be eligible to return to full-time PGA Tour membership status before 2028.

Brian Rolapp, speaking for the first time since LIV Golf officially entered into bankruptcy proceedings in federal court, told reporters on Tuesday, Sept. 15, the PGA Tour is not offering the path Brooks Koepka used to come back from LIV Golf before the 2026 season. Rolapp emphasized meritocracy, membership rules, accountability and discipline as "guiding principles for us," as the PGA Tour transitions to a new competition model after next season.

Golf.body:
No, Jon Rahm says, he isn’t “fed up” with being asked about LIV Golf. No, he said, he still couldn’t reveal whether he could leave LIV, outside of saying “there’s a long legal process.”

But no, he said, he probably won’t be involved in “the politics of the game” going forward. Speaking Tuesday ahead of this week’s BMW PGA Championship on the DP World Tour, Rahm said that’s been a lesson learned, and it comes as LIV, the tour on which he’s played since 2024, seeks to stay alive following the departure of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund.

Golf.title: At one of golf's most unique events, 80 juniors get a shot on the big stage
Golf.summary: This week, 80 First Tee participants and 80 PGA Tour Champions pros will team up to compete for the title at the Pure Insurance Championship. The post At one of golf’s most unique events, 80 juniors get a shot on the big stage appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
This week, Pebble Beach hosts one of the coolest events in golf — and most people don’t even know it’s happening. The PURE Insurance Championship gets underway at one of golf’s most iconic venues on Friday, bringing together one of the most unique fields you’ll see all season. Here’s what you should know about it.

This week, 80 First Tee participants, 80 PGA Tour Champions pros and 160 amateurs team up to compete in a 54-hole best-ball format for the pro-junior title. For most of the non-pros, it will be their first time playing Pebble Beach, and they come from all over the states — 52 First Tee chapters from across the country have sent players to compete.

Golf.title: Don't make this crucial set-up mistake when hitting bunker shots
Golf.summary: In the first episode of Top 100 Teacher Sessions, David Armitage explains how to set up for success in the bunkers. The post Don’t make this crucial set-up mistake when hitting bunker shots appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The bunker is a scary place for many recreational golfers. When players with a bunker-phobia find the sand, they typically have one thought in mind: “Don’t screw this up.” The problem with that mindset is that it introduces doubt and leads to hesitant swings, which is never a good strategy in the trap.

The reason for their doubt and hesitation is a history of poor play from the sand. When you’ve spent your career either blading it long or chunking it in front of your feet, there’s little reason for optimism.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: Do I get free relief if my ball hits a fake bird?
Golf.summary: What should you do if your ball hits a bird decoy on the course? Are you entitled to free relief? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: Do I get free relief if my ball hits a fake bird? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’’e got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. To scare waterfowl away from the lake shores, our course uses fake birds on slender poles attached by string and wire that can “fly” with the breeze—soaring, dipping, turning, and so on. A few of these fake birds can be in the line of play from a tee box or near a green. What happens if a shot hits one of these “birds”? It is possible to take the pole out of the ground, play the shot, and replace the pole before hitting, though this can slow the pace of play quite a bit. Movable obstruction? Immovable? Help! —Bill Spahn, via email

You’re trying to sneak in a multipart question, Bill! We’re almost rooting for the waterfowl at this point. As to the first question, if you play near one of those “birds” and hit one, you’ll have to play the ball as it lies — no different than bouncing off a moving cart or a stationary pole, per Rule 11.1.

Golf.title: PGA Tour rules out return programme for LIV Golf players after bankruptcy protection filing
Golf.summary: PGA Tour rules out return programme for LIV Golf players after bankruptcy protection filing The Independent
Golf.body:
There are currently no plans for a route allowing LIV Golf players to return to the US-based PGA Tour, Commissioner Brian Rolapp stated on Tuesday, ruling out a mechanism similar to the one that enabled Brooks Koepka to rejoin earlier this year.

Speaking to journalists during a virtual media call one week after LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, Rolapp insisted that discipline and accountability are vital components for any sporting league and remain core guiding principles for the PGA Tour.

Golf.title: The reason why LIV Golf's future is holding up a DP World Tour pathway to the PGA Tour's new model
Golf.summary: The reason why LIV Golf's future is holding up a DP World Tour pathway to the PGA Tour's new model Golf Digest
Golf.body:
There was a lot of specificity in the PGA Tour’s Tuesday announcement about future membership criteria towards its two-tiered future. Which made the lack of information towards one group somewhat noteworthy.

The PGA Tour is five years into a strategic alliance with its European counterpart, the DP World Tour, a move largely made to financially support the Old World circuit following the pandemic while combating the looming threat of LIV Golf. An upshot of that agreement was a pathway for the top 10 DP World Tour members to graduate to the PGA Tour, an exemption that has been used by the likes of Robert MacIntyre, Min Woo Lee, Matthieu Pavon and Rasmus Hojgaard.

Golf.summary: Why Jon Rahm has no involvement in huge LIV Golf changes Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm was asked about his LIV Golf future once again at the BMW PGA Championship. His response was telling… It was Groundhog Day as Jon Rahm faced the media at the BMW PGA Championship. The burning questions at Wentworth, of course, concerned the uncertain futures of both the Spaniard and LIV Golf – and Rahm once again failed to commit to the beleaguered league.

When asked if he is fed up with the constant inquisition, Rahm allowed a wry smile. “I understand you’re all doing your job, I get it,” he said, before adding: “I’m liking that you all see the humor in this at this point.” But Rahm also confirmed that “nothing has changed”.

Golf.title: How to stop sliding during the downswing for better ball striking
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Mark Durland explains why sliding during the downswing hurts your ball striking — and how to fix it. The post How to stop sliding during the downswing for better ball striking appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the most common trends I see among mid-handicap golfers is a tendency to slide through the downswing rather than rotate. This can create several seemingly unrelated problems such as poor driver performance, inconsistent iron compression, a steep angle of attack, and an excessively inside-out club path that produces blocks and over-hooks.

The golf swing is a blend of three forces: vertical, lateral, and rotational. Every golfer uses all three, but problems arise when those forces become unbalanced. For this type of player, there is often too much lateral movement and not enough rotation.

Golf.title: LIV golfer calls out ‘rat’ in player group chat, upset with confidential leaks
Golf.summary: LIV golfer calls out ‘rat’ in player group chat, upset with confidential leaks Golf Digest
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has been a lot of things: A much-discussed lightning rod, a fountain of money (until recently) and a ratings disaster. Well, now, we can add one more thing to the list—a league with a snitch, à la The Departed.

While speaking to Ben Parsons at Today’s Golfer, LIV golfer and 2025 WM Phoenix Open winner Thomas Detry revealed that he thinks there’s a “rat” in the player group chat who’s been leaking information to the media. The once-Saudi-backed league is clearly in some financial struggles right now, and Detry admitted to some frustration with a yet-to-be-determined pro who keeps betraying his fellow players’ trust as they try to ride out this wave.

Golf.title: The 2026 PGA Tour's winningest putters show mallets are the new king
Golf.summary: The TaylorMade Spider was again the winningest putter on the PGA Tour, but mallets in general were nearly unbeatable. The post The 2026 PGA Tour’s winningest putters show mallets are the new king appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you were to describe the list of PGA Tour winning putters with two words, the first would easily be “mallet.” Across 37 events with 38 winners, only five events by three different pros were won all season by a blade putter. Matt Fitzpatrick won three times with his Bettinardi blade while Tom Kim and Ryan Fox made it a blade sweep in the PGA Tour’s two links golf events, the Scottish Open and Open Championship.

Other than that, every other event this season was won by players using mallet putters. Nine of those players, combining for 13 wins, were using TaylorMade Spider family putters and 11 of them were using the flagship Spider Tour X. The 11 wins for the Spider Tour X shape were more than any other putter brand this season.

Golf.title: Cabot is building a second golf resort in Nova Scotia. Here's what we know
Golf.summary: Cabot, the luxury developer of golf courses and real estate, is doubling down on the Canadian province where the company was born. The post Cabot is building a second golf resort in Nova Scotia. Here’s what we know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In 1497, the navigator John Cabot, fresh off explorations of eastern Canada, returned to England to a hero’s welcome. More than 500 years later, a global brand that bears his name is planning a homecoming of a different kind.

Cabot, the prominent golf and real-estate developer with a portfolio of marquee properties around the world, on Monday announced its latest project: Cabot Wilds, a destination resort in Nova Scotia anchored by an 18-hole course from Canadian architect Jeff Mingay, set to open in late 2027. The project is being developed in partnership with Canadian businessman John Bragg, a longtime Cabot investor who recently increased his stake in the company.

Golf.title: How youth helped Nordqvist answer critics and deliver Solheim Cup win
Golf.summary: Captain Anna Nordqvist's faith in Europe's young rookies paid off as they delivered crucial points in regaining the Solheim Cup with victory over the United States, writes Iain Carter.
Golf.body:
Anna Nordqvist spoke in the build-up to the Solheim Cup about the European team being in a period of transition as she chose a line-up with four debutants. Any fears about fielding rookies for the most pressure packed event in the women's game were proven unfounded in her team's thrilling 15-13 victory at Bernardus Golf last weekend.

Nastasia Nadaud (21), Julia Lopez Ramirez (23), Mimi Rhodes (24) and, eventually, Lottie Woad all delivered crucial points and gave an encouraging glimpse into Europe's future.

Golf.title: U.S. Solheim Cup team was riding a high. Then came Sunday singles
Golf.summary: The Americans celebrated with beers after Saturday at the Solheim Cup. But the Europeans wound up popping the champagne. The post U.S. Solheim Cup team was riding a high. Then came Sunday singles appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The wheels on the bus go round and round. The questions about the bus keep coming, too. The U.S. team bus at the Solheim Cup, that is. They first arose on Saturday evening in the Netherlands, when Team USA erupted in sudsy celebration of Jennifer Kupcho’s fourball heroics, which had turned around the day’s last match. What had looked like a sure deficit heading into Sunday was now deadlocked, and the Americans were in a festive mood.

Out came beers on the team bus. As videos of the moment swirled on social media, so did questions — and criticism — from online commentators. Wasn’t it too early to celebrate? How did the optics look? Might the boozy antics lead to a letdown? Provide the Europeans with extra motivation?

Golf.title: 'I can't believe it'
Golf.summary: Shane Lowry produces a frontrunning masterclass to cruise to a record 11-shot win at the Irish Open and end his four-year wait for an individual title in emphatic style.
Golf.body:

Shane Lowry produced a frontrunning masterclass to clinch a record 11-shot win at the Irish Open and end his four-year wait for an individual title in emphatic style. Golf.title: Here's where the next Solheim Cup will be played in 2028
Golf.summary: As the 2026 Solheim Cup finishes up in the Netherlands, next up will be 2028 in the United States. Here's a look at past and future venues. The post Here’s where the next Solheim Cup will be played in 2028 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The 2026 Solheim Cup finishes this weekend in the Netherlands, which means you’ll have to wait two more years before the next iteration of the biennial event arrives. Although in 2028 it returns to the U.S.

Next up is Valhalla Golf Club in Louisville, Ky., to host the 21st playing of the Solheim Cup come Sept. 8-10, 2028. Valhalla is no stranger to golf’s marquee events. It’s hosted four PGA Championships, two Senior PGA Championships and the 2008 Ryder Cup. It most recently hosted the 2024 PGA, which was won by Xander Schauffele but perhaps most remembered for the bizarre arrest of World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler.

Golf.title: After posting his most lucrative season to date, Jake Knapp has sights set on majors
Golf.summary: Nine top-25 finishes made 2026 Jake Knapp's most lucrative Tour season to date. But the 32-year-old is focusing on loftier goals. The post After posting his most lucrative season to date, Jake Knapp has sights set on majors appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
At 32, he’s not your typical “new” PGA Tour star, but he definitely played like one this season. Dylan Dethier: You played some really good golf in 2026 — 11th or better in seven of your first eight starts this season, including the Masters. What does it feel like to be on a run like that?

Jake Knapp: I mean, obviously it feels good. It doesn’t feel, like, crazy different; it’s not like I’m hitting it exactly where I want to on every shot or making every putt or chipping in all the time. I just think I did a job good this offseason analyzing what areas I could really benefit from the most — maximizing my practice time, locking in on ball striking — and seeing improvement has been great. Obviously, when you’re playing well, you want to try to take advantage and win, but when you put yourself in contention as often as you can that’s uplifting too. Because golf is golf; you’re going to have some weird stuff happen. But when it does you know that it’s, like, Hey, I’m playing fine. That’s the sign, really, that your work is kind of coming to fruition and then you see it show up with results.

Despite being caught by Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen, Lowry one-putted every green on the back nine in a five-under 65 to maintain control of the tournament. "I'm normally the one watching other people do it, so why not me sometimes," Lowry said when asked about his joy on the greens.

Golf.title: Jennifer Kupcho's late heroics flip the script at Solheim Cup
Golf.summary: At the Solheim Cup Saturday, 2 birdie bombs by Jennifer Kupcho helped tie the match at 8-8 heading into Sunday singles. The post Jennifer Kupcho’s late heroics flip the script at Solheim Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Jennifer Kupcho cupped a hand to her ear toward the grandstands, then raised a finger to her lips to shush the gallery further. The quiet that fell over the crowd stood in stark contrast to the pyrotechnics Kupcho had just provided on a taut Saturday at the Solheim Cup. Paired with Lindy Duncan and down a hole with two to play, Kupcho birdied both 17 and 18, completing a remarkable comeback and stealing a point from Céline Boutier and Carlota Ciganda.

The win gave the Americans a 3-1 edge in the afternoon fourballs and brought the competition level heading into Sunday singles, with the teams tied 8-8. “I don’t know, walking up to the green, honestly, like, I just thought, like, OK, during all these practice rounds, I’d just get up and whack it,” Kupcho said. “So, yeah, really didn’t read it. I was, like, all right, we’ll just give it a run, make sure we get it there, but what the heck it went in. That was insane.”

Golf.title: Finally, after four years and $5.5 billion, LIV Golf isn’t only morally bankrupt | Opinion
Golf.summary: Finally, after four years and $5.5 billion, LIV Golf isn’t only morally bankrupt | Opinion Golfweek
Golf.body:
Finally, after four years and $5.5 billion, LIV Golf isn’t only morally bankrupt | Opinion There’s likely to be more poetry than justice in the poetic justice of LIV Golf facing financial insolvency that complements its moral bankruptcy, since it won’t only be the deserving players and agents who’ll be stiffed on invoices but also vendors and employees who can ill afford the hit.

For poetry, we can enjoy how the Chapter 11 filing blows away the smokescreen of obfuscation and guff that has governed LIV’s dealings since launch, forcing the league to cite real-world figures and facts. Like admitting that the Saudi Public Investment Fund lost $5 billion and would fund the 2026 season only with a $495 million loan, which was still insufficient to cover the schedule without canceling two tournaments. Or that only $15 million cash remains on hand from that near $5.5 billion. Or that LIV’s media rights deal was worth a paltry $5 million, equivalent to revenue earned selling team merchandise. Or that executives averaged $250,000 in annual credit card bills. Or that LIV shorted the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees $1.7 million, money promised in support of its mission to aid displaced peoples, presumably including those impacted by the Saudi involvement in Sudan. (Pity the many social media bootlickers who beclowned themselves daily and didn’t even earn a spot on the creditors list.)

Golf.title: The Solheim Cup venue isn't a 'club' or 'course.' Here's why
Golf.summary: Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, host of the 2026 Solheim Cup, is a high-end property and a smartly cultivated brand. The post The Solheim Cup venue isn’t a ‘club’ or ‘course.’ Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
What’s in a name? At this week’s Solheim Cup in the Netherlands, the question gives us plenty to unpack. The host venue is Bernardus Golf, a name that’s notable for what’s not in it. No mention of “club.” No reference to “course.”

Robert van der Wallen, the Dutch entrepreneur who developed Bernardus, set out to create an upscale members’ enclave without the starchy trappings of a country club. He wanted the property to feel exclusive. He didn’t want it to be off limits. So he omitted “club,” with its closed-circle connotations. And he left out “course,” with its utilitarian implications. What remained — Bernardus Golf — has the ring of a lifestyle brand, an experience anyone can access.

Golf.title: The Harbor Course at Wild Dunes is teeming with history and lowcountry charm

Golf.body:
Tucked away on Isle of Palms is Wild Dunes, a lowcountry South Carolina golf retreat that seems to have it all: towering live oaks draped in Spanish moss, palmettos that frame the greens, marshland stretching along nearby fairways and the glittering Atlantic just beyond the dunes.

It’s the kind of coastal scene that makes you slow down so much that you almost forget you’re supposed to be keeping score. The Harbor Course, however, has a way of bringing you back to the task at hand.

Golf.body:
A dominating performance from Americans Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin was the only thing that stood between the Europeans and an early morning foursomes sweep on Saturday at the Solheim Cup.

Europe won the first three matches of Day 2 at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands to take a 7-5 lead. “We don’t like being down, but look, I think this afternoon is really important,” said U.S. captain Angela Stanford. “It’s going to be the toughest session because it’s probably the most fans we have seen out here. They’re getting rowdy. So this is going to be a really tough afternoon. And I told them it’s going to be tough. So hopefully they’re up for it.”

Golf.title: How this new putting 'toolkit' can make you better on the greens
Golf.summary: The Trigon Toolkit from Short Game Gains features four different tools that can help you improve your alignment, start line and more. The post How this new putting ‘toolkit’ can make you better on the greens appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When it comes to putting practice, I’ve always found that a little additional structure can make a significant difference. Using training aids or tools that provide feedback on setup keys and other important details gives my practice more purpose — and ultimately helps me become a more reliable putter under pressure.

That’s why I was interested in trying the Trigon Toolkit from Short Game Gains. I’ve been using their steel putting mirror for the past year or so, and it has become a regular part of my practice routine. The new Trigon Toolkit builds on that same idea by combining several simple putting tools to address different aspects of putting.

Golf.title: Want to hit wedges that spin? Try this simple tee drill
Golf.summary: Top 100 Teacher John Scott Rattan is often asked how to hit chips that spin. Here, he explains how to practice the shot with a simple drill. The post Want to hit wedges that spin? Try this simple tee drill appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the most common questions I get is how to hit a wedge that sucks back on the green. You know, the one that bounces past the hole, stops and spins back close to the pin. In reality, it’s a pretty simple shot to hit. Most techniques in the golf swing work in pairs, and flighted scoring clubs are no different. If we can manage the clubface and loft early in the swing, impact becomes a by-product.

One of the best ways to practice this is by placing a golf tee in your lead hand between your middle and ring fingers, all the way at the base. Make your backswing and feel like you’re twisting the tee behind you in transition.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Leaderboard At The Amgen Irish Open: Big Names Well Placed Heading Into The Weekend
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Leaderboard At The Amgen Irish Open: Big Names Well Placed Heading Into The Weekend Golf Monthly
Golf.body:
Shane Lowry's sparkling second-round 62, a course record at Trump International Doonbeg, has given the chasing pack lots of work to do over the weekend. Several big names remain in touch and, among those hoping to chase down the home favorite, are multiple LIV Golfers, including Jon Rahm, Joaquin Niemann, Adrian Meronk, and Tom McKibbin.

However, of the nine LIV players to tee it up in Ireland, there were also a few surprise missed cuts, especially Tyrrell Hatton, an eight-time winner on the DP World Tour. The Englishman, who would have fancied his chances heading to Ireland, was out of sorts on Thursday, shooting an eight-over-par 78.

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s bleak future shifts to the courtroom
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s bleak future shifts to the courtroom Financial Times
Golf.body:
The NFL’s international slate kicked off on Thursday night (or Friday morning, depending on your point of view), with victory for the San Francisco 49ers over the Los Angeles Rams inside Melbourne Cricket Ground.

This was the first NFL regular season game to take place in Australia, and breaks new ground for the league’s global ambitions. Attendance of just over 100,000 makes it the seventh biggest crowd in NFL history, while the game was also beamed globally on Netflix, building on the success of the streamer’s Christmas Day broadcasts.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy played his slowest-ever round. Then came different kind of test
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy's Irish Open defense got off to a slow start. His opening round took six hours, and Friday brought more challenges. The post Rory McIlroy played his slowest-ever round. Then came different kind of test appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
“I can’t recall a round of golf that has taken that long before. We’ve had some rounds that are five-and-a-half or five-and-three-quarter hours, but six hours is a first for me.”

McIlroy wasn’t being hyperbolic. He and his playing partners, Robert MacIntyre and Brooks Koepka, had started their round at Doonbeg, on Ireland’s southwest coast, at 1:35 p.m. local time. Their group’s final putt dropped at 7:41, meaning their round clocked in at a cool 6 hours and 6 minutes, or roughly the same time it takes to fly from New York to Dublin.

Golf.title: Phil Mickelson revelation comes to light just days after shock LIV Golf bankruptcy news
Golf.summary: Phil Mickelson revelation comes to light just days after shock LIV Golf bankruptcy news Golfmagic
Golf.body:
A fresh revelation surrounding Phil Mickelson has emerged just days after LIV Golf stunned the sport by filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. According to Sportico, Mickelson reportedly owned a 0.23% stake in LIV Golf when the Saudi-backed circuit entered bankruptcy proceedings, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The revelation follows the publication of LIV’s 128-page filing in the District of New Jersey, which provided a rare insight into the ownership structure behind the controversial breakaway tour.

Golf.title: Fred Couples' coolest shot ever? He might've just hit it
Golf.summary: Fred Couples is the coolest man in golf — and he just added to his lore with an insane chip-in at the Sanford International. The post Fred Couples’ coolest shot ever? He might’ve just hit it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Fred Couples may be the coolest man in golf. And at this week’s Sanford International, he added to that lore. At a Wednesday evening sponsor outing ahead of the event, there was a closest-to-the pin shootout from just off the green. Of course, Couples was the winner of the shootout — but it was how he won that is the stuff of legends.

With daylight fading over the clubhouse, Couples stepped up to his pitch and, with as smooth an action as ever, lofted his ball onto the green. As the ball rolled toward the hole, Couples turned around and started interacting with those around him.

Golf.title: GOLF Magazine announces 2026 World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame inductees
Golf.summary: The 2026 World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame inductees include Todd Anderson, Martin Hall, Ted Sheftic and the late Dana Rader. The post GOLF Magazine announces 2026 World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame inductees appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
GOLF Magazine this week announced its 2026 class for the World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame. The inductees include Todd Anderson, Martin Hall, Ted Sheftic and the late Dana Rader.

These inductees will be honored at the 2026 GOLF Top 100 Teachers Summit, which will take place Nov. 1-4 at the Omni La Costa Resort & Spa in Carlsbad, Calif. “Each of the instructors we have chosen to enter the World Golf Teachers Hall of Fame this year has earned the distinction in their own unique way,” said Hoyt McGarity, CEO and President of 8AM Golf, the parent company of GOLF Magazine and GOLF.com. “The groundbreaking efforts and longevity of the careers of Todd, Martin, Ted, and Dana are something to behold and it’s an honor to recognize each of them for their extraordinary contributions.”

Golf.summary: This Solheim Cup is already tense. Thanks to an epic closing putt from Carlota Ciganda, an all-time match is brewing. The post With 1 epic putt, an all-time Solheim Cup is brewing in the Netherlands appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
This article was all set to have a different headline. It was ready to praise the top American players who have dominated the Solheim Cup for years, and who are very much doing so again.

But then Carlota Ciganda stepped in over her ball, roughly 15 feet from the cup and drilled the putt, center of the jar, halving the final match of the second session and keeping the Cup tied through Day 1 for just the second time in its 36-year history.

Golf.title: Ciganda's late sparkle lifts Europe on dramatic opening day of Solheim Cup
Golf.summary: Carlota Ciganda steals the show after Europe's top pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad fail to ignite on day one of the Solheim Cup against the United States.
Golf.body:
Carlota Ciganda once again stole the show after Europe's top pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad failed to ignite against the USA on the opening day of the Solheim Cup. The 36-year-old Spaniard - the oldest player competing this weekend - let out a roar after holing a 15-foot putt to earn Europe an unlikely half point in the final fourball match of the day and ensure honours are even at 4-4.

Ciganda's celebration evoked memories of the nerve-shredding finale at Finca Cortesin in 2023, when her putt allowed Europe to retain the trophy with a 14-14 tie. And once again Nelly Korda, beaten by Ciganda in Spain three years ago, was on the receiving end.

Golf.title: 2026 Solheim Cup Saturday pairings, matches, tee times, TV schedule
Golf.summary: The 2026 Solheim Cup continues Saturday in the Netherlands. Here are the pairings for the morning foursomes matches and info on how to watch. The post 2026 Solheim Cup Saturday pairings, matches, tee times, TV schedule appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Eight matches played. Four points for the United States. Four points for the Europeans. If there’s anything we learned after Friday’s first-day play at the Solheim Cup, it’s that the next two days should be good at Bernardus Golf course in the Netherlands.

The biggest drama on Friday was saved for the very end. On the par-4 18, the European duo of Carlota Ciganda and Julia Lopez Ramirez and Americans Nelly Korda and Lauren Coughlin were all square in their four-ball match — and Ciganda’s clubface on the tee wasn’t square. She went right. On her second shot, she played up the adjacent first hole. From right of the green with her third shot, she pitched to 10 feet. Ahead of her, the Americans were in with a par, and Lopez Ramirez bogeyed.

Golf.title: The Solheim Cup, now 20 editions old, owes much to its namesake
Golf.summary: You might have heard the Ryder Cup is named for British seed merchant Samuel Ryder. The Solheim Cup’s origin story is less well known. The post The Solheim Cup, now 20 editions old, owes much to its namesake appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Everyone seems to know that the Ryder Cup is named for — altogether now — the British seed merchant Samuel Ryder, who donated the trophy. But how many people know that the Solheim Cup is named for a transplanted Norwegian named Karsten Solheim, who started making a pinging putter in a garage in Phoenix that eventually became an innovative club-manufacturing empire known throughout golfdom as Ping, a division of Karsten Manufacturing?

“We gave them three options for the name of the event,” John Solheim, one of Karsten’s sons, now in his early 80s, said the other day. His them was the organizing bodies that put on the Solheim Cup, the LPGA and the LET, the Ladies’ European Tour. “Solheim Cup, Karsten Cup or Ping Cup. I’m glad they went with Solheim.”

Golf.title: How great college players become great pros, according to a top college coach
Golf.summary: Matt Thurmond of ASU men's golf has built a career on building good men first and Tour stars second. The challenges of that may surprise you. The post How great college players become great pros, according to a top college coach appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Every time I walk the range at a big amateur event or spend time testing with elite college kids, I see the same thing: launch monitor numbers that would make half the guys in the top 50 in the world blush.

Ball speed that jumps off the face. Efficiency numbers through the roof. Perfect wedge gaps. To the untrained eye, the conclusion is simple: How is this kid not walking directly onto the PGA Tour tomorrow?

Golf.title: LIV Golf Winner Makes Late Charge At Q School To Join Fellow Players In Next Stage
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Winner Makes Late Charge At Q School To Join Fellow Players In Next Stage Golf Monthly
Golf.body:
With LIV Golf’s future shrouded in uncertainty, several of its players have been attempting to earn DP World Tour cards via the first stage of Q School. Earlier in the month in Huddersfield, England, Josele Ballester and Luis Masaveu moved on to the second stage, which begins in Spain in late October, while Peter Uihlein was disqualified from the event after failing to show up to his third-round tee time.

A week later, another first stage qualifier was held at Seddiner See in Michendorf, Germany, where HyFlyers GC’s Michael La Sasso and LIV Golf wild card Yosuke Asaji were in the field.

Golf.title: This Dallas Cowboys-themed golf course just got a $12 million makeover
Golf.summary: A recently completed multimillion-dollar redo has transformed Cowboys Golf Club into a varied, family-friendly entertainment venue. The post This Dallas Cowboys-themed golf course just got a $12 million makeover appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As the placekicker for the Dallas Cowboys, Brandon Aubrey has leg enough for field goals of nearly 70 yards. In practice, though, he’s been known to aim at uprights from more than twice as far. That’s not on the gridiron. It’s at the driving range on a property unlike any other — Cowboys Golf Club, the only NFL-themed golf course in the world.

Like the famous franchise it celebrates, the club has ties to Cowboys owner Jerry Jones, who opened it in 2001, cutting the ribbon on a clubhouse filled with team memorabilia and a championship layout with white-sand bunkers and a giant blue star in one of its fairways.

Golf.title: These versatile pieces of apparel made packing for my golf trip a breeze
Golf.summary: When a golf trip called for fashionable, functional pieces that easily transitioned from on course to off, TravisMathew came to the rescue. The post These versatile pieces of apparel made packing for my golf trip a breeze appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Readers of this space may recall that I am a staunch proponent of carry-on luggage. I have come to believe, no matter the length of your trip, if it involves air travel, traveling with a carry-on is a non-negotiable. I managed to do it on a two-week international trip for the last two years, which helped me feel empowered to limit myself to a carry-on for every subsequent trip since, regardless of the destination.

That is, until I had a golf trip on the horizon. Uh oh. The trip was only three days, but the variety of outfits required — travel apparel, on- and off-course options, post-golf attire, and multiple pairs of shoes, of course — had me doubting myself. How could a carry-on provide all of the packing space I needed? The solution was obvious: I needed to bring clothes that work just as well on the course as they do off. But that strategy brought another problem to the surface: Multi-functional golf apparel that functions well on the course and looks suitable off it is notoriously hard to find — especially for women.

How could a carry-on provide all of the packing space I needed? The solution was obvious: I needed to bring clothes that work just as well on the course as they do off. But that strategy brought another problem to the surface: Multi-functional golf apparel that functions well on the course and looks suitable off it is notoriously hard to find — especially for women.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Loses a Golf State
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Loses a Golf State VideoAge International
Golf.body:
The golf league LIV Golf, founded to challenge the American PGA Tour, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, with up to $1 billion in liabilities, after its primary backer, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), pulled its funding four years after LIV was founded. The Gulf state had poured some $5 billion into the LIV Golf venture.

Reportedly, the league’s top seven creditors are LIV players themselves. However, PIF is providing a $49.6 million loan to fund the bankruptcy proceedings, while LIV is seeking $300 million in additional investment to keep the golf league going.

Golf.body:
Greg Norman has admitted LIV Golf got one of its biggest strategic decisions wrong from the outset, while insisting he never intended to destroy the PGA Tour. Golf.title: Mickelson Is Unnamed Player-Shareholder in LIV Golf Filing
Golf.summary: Mickelson Is Unnamed Player-Shareholder in LIV Golf Filing Sportico.com
Golf.body:
Phil Mickelson owned a 0.23% stake in LIV Golf at the time of its bankruptcy filings, according to a person familiar with the matter. On Tuesday, LIV Golf submitted a 128-page document to tee off its Chapter 11 proceedings in the District of New Jersey, outlining financial details such as the cap table of the tour. LIV Golf had issued 98.48% of its common ownership to the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, 1.05% to Performance54 Group Limited, an entity controlled by PIF, and 0.23% to former CEO Greg Norman. The document also noted a 0.23% stake held by a “current player.”

The identity of the unnamed golfer is Mickelson, said the person, who was granted anonymity because the matter is private. LIV Golf declined to comment. A representative for Mickelson did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

Badminton.title: History Watch: Two Museums, Two Approaches
Badminton.summary: History Watch: Two Museums, Two Approaches BWF
Badminton.body:
August was a good month for the conservation of badminton heritage, with two museums opening in Europe just a day apart – one in Germany, the other in Denmark. Quite significantly, they are the first badminton museums in either country.

Badminton Museum Bonn, located in the premises of Badminton Club Beuel (Germany’s biggest club), showcases the personal collection of former players and history enthusiasts Helga and Roland Maywald, and opened on 29 August. While most badminton museums celebrate the competition aspect of the sport (players, tournaments), the Maywalds’ collection is devoted to preserving badminton’s presence in the everyday lives of people over the past few centuries, through historical artefacts such as porcelain figurines, postcards, paintings, etc.

Badminton.title: ‘I Want to be a Legend’
Badminton.summary: ‘I Want to be a Legend’ BWF
Badminton.body:
Winning, and making history along the way, has become almost routine for An Se Young. The world No.1 has already collected seven individual titles this season, putting her on course to eclipse the record-equalling 11 she won last year. Yet, she heads into next week’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with her focus firmly on the next match rather than the numbers piling up behind her.

“Records make you a legend. I want to be a legend in badminton,” An said. “But also, they mean you keep improving yourself. So it makes me more motivated. “I always think I can improve further because my rivals could catch up and overtake me. I never take any match for granted.”

Taiwan’s Chen Zhi-ray and Lin Yu-chieh won the men’s doubles final at the Yonex-Sunrise Vietnam Open badminton tournament on Sunday, dispatching their Singaporean opponents in 27 minutes in back-to-back games.

Badminton.title: Behind the Mic, Matsuyama Finds Reprieve
Badminton.summary: Behind the Mic, Matsuyama Finds Reprieve BWF
Badminton.body:
Nami Matsuyama has spent years experiencing the Japan Open from the court. This year, she saw it from behind the microphone. Recovering from ACL surgery, the doubles specialist made an unexpected Japan Open debut in a new role, joining broadcaster J Sports as a colour commentator for the mixed doubles match featuring her regular partner Hiroki Midorikawa and Olympic champion Misaki Matsutomo.

For Matsuyama, the assignment was the realisation of a long-held ambition and a chance to discover a different side of the sport she knows so well. “This is one of my dreams,” she said. “I just wanted to try this and today I did it.”

Competitor News.summary: Deutsche Bank links up with Singapore Open in four-year title partnership sportsmintmedia.com
Competitor News.body:
Deutsche Bank has signed a multi-year agreement to become the title partner of the Singapore Open through 2029, giving the historic Asian golf tournament a major international financial-services brand as it returns to the DP World Tour schedule in 2027.

The event will be jointly sanctioned by the DP World Tour and Asian Tour and will form part of the DP World Tour’s 2027 Asian Swing and the opening phase of the Race to Dubai.

Competitor News.title: Sentosa to Host 2027 Deutsche Bank Singapore Open Under Landmark DP World Tour and Asian Tour Partnership
Competitor News.summary: Sentosa to Host 2027 Deutsche Bank Singapore Open Under Landmark DP World Tour and Asian Tour Partnership Golf Industry Asia
Competitor News.body:
The Deutsche Bank Singapore Open will return to Sentosa Golf Club’s Serapong course from 15–18 April 2027 as a co-sanctioned event between the DP World Tour and Asian Tour. The announcement confirms Sentosa’s continued status as one of Asia’s leading championship venues. Earlier in 2026, the club hosted three major championships, including the Singapore Open, within an eight-week window. The course has long been recognised for its championship conditioning, Tournament Ready 365 (TR365) agronomy programme and industry-leading sustainability practices.

The Singapore Open first came to The Serapong on the Asian Tour in 2005, when Adam Scott claimed the first of his three titles there. Between 2009 and 2012 the event was co-sanctioned by the European Tour (now DP World Tour) and Asian Tour. After a four-year absence, the tournament returned to Sentosa in April 2026.

Competitor News.title: Metro Bank launches new payments partnership to help businesses with cashflow
Competitor News.summary: Metro Bank launches new payments partnership to help businesses with cashflow FStech
Competitor News.body:
Metro Bank has launched a new partnership with payments provider Elavon, giving its business customers access to a wider range of payment technologies designed to improve cashflow management and simplify how they accept payments.

The collaboration will provide businesses ranging from sole traders to large corporates with payment solutions across in-store, online and remote channels, including fixed and mobile card terminals, electronic point of sale (EPOS) systems, and online and telephone payment services.

Competitor News.summary: Five decades of supporting tennis: BNP Paribas returns to back star-studded Singapore Open The Business Times
Competitor News.body:
[SINGAPORE] Some of the world’s top female tennis players – including Filipino sensation Alexandra Eala – will be making their way to Singapore soon for a high-profile tournament that comes with a prize pool of US$1.25 million.

The Singapore Tennis Open (STO) presented by BNP Paribas takes place from Sep 21 to 27 at The Kallang’s OCBC Arena, with this being the only WTA 500 event in South-east Asia this season.

Competitor News.title: Turkish Airlines to Replace Standard Chartered on Liverpool Shirts
Competitor News.summary: Turkish Airlines to Replace Standard Chartered on Liverpool Shirts MarketScale
Competitor News.body:
Sports Business Journal reported Turkish Airlines agreed a five-year, roughly $405 million deal (about $81 million a year) to become Liverpool's main shirt sponsor starting in the 2027-28 season, replacing Standard Chartered. The same week, SportBusiness reported Infront sold its 60% stake in Hyrox to a consortium led by L Catterton at a valuation of about €600 million, and SportBusiness Sponsorship reported Newcastle United is projected to earn more than £70 million a year from its main sponsorship inventory by 2027-28.
